sights.description: The Yoshimura Residence preserves the architectural style of the Momoyama period's Shoin-zukuri architecture.

sights.name: Tsuboi Hachiman Shrine
sights.description: Tsuboi Hachiman Shrine, located at the southern end of Habikino City, is the guardian deity of the Kawachi Genji clan, the ancestors of Minamoto no Yoritomo, who founded the Kamakura Shogunate.

sights.name: Daikokuji Temple
sights.description: Founded by En no Ascetic in 665, this is the first sacred site in Japan where Daikokuten appears. It is widely worshipped as the birthplace of Daikokuten, the god of fortune, and also as a sacred site for the Seven Lucky Gods and the Kawachi Saigoku Kannon Temple.

sights.name: Morimoto Shrine
sights.description: Located in Habikino City, Osaka Prefecture, this shrine enshrines the husband and wife deities Futsunushi-no-Mikoto and Futsunushi-hime-no-Mikoto.

sights.name: Kawachi Konda Haniwa Village Okuraya
sights.description: This is a haniwa-making experience facility located in Habikino City, Osaka Prefecture, where haniwa making was popular 1,500 years ago. There is also a shop and gallery selling kofun and haniwa goods, and you can also enjoy original haniwa bento lunches.

sights.name: Suichoen Ruins Park
sights.description: This park was developed around the Suichoen archaeological site, where traces of stone tool making from the Paleolithic period, dating back 20,000 years, were discovered. Known as a stone tool making atelier, visitors can learn about the conditions of that time through videos and exhibits.

sights.name: Sairinji Temple
sights.description: Located in Habikino City, Osaka Prefecture, this historic temple is said to have been founded by a descendant of the Baekje scholar, Dr. Wang In.

sights.name: Konda Hachimangu Shrine
sights.description: Japan's oldest Hachiman Shrine is located south of the Konda Gobyoyama Kofun (the tomb of Emperor Ojin) in Habikino City, Osaka Prefecture. It is said to have been built by order of Emperor Kinmei in the late 6th century, and houses a portable shrine, a national treasure, among other items.

sights.name: Nonakaji Temple
sights.description: Counted as one of the "Three Princes of Kawachi," this temple was built during the Asuka period and is associated with Prince Shotoku.

sights.name: Ryotaro Shiba Memorial Museum
sights.description: This memorial museum conveys the spirit of author Ryotaro Shiba to future generations. The approximately 2,600 square meter site is adjacent to Shiba's home and the memorial museum, designed by Tadao Ando.

sights.name: Osaka Prefectural Central Library
sights.description: Osaka Prefectural Central Library, which boasts the largest collection of books in Osaka, opened in Higashiosaka City in 1996.

sights.name: Prefectural Forest (Kusaka Park)
sights.description: A nature park (total 9 locations in prefecture) that has forests and facilities maintained by the Osaka government to commemorate the 100 year anniversary of the prefecture and for visitors to enjoy the rich nature of Kongo-Ikoma-Kisen Quasi-National Park.

sights.name: Forest of Osaka (Narukawa park)
sights.description: This natural park is home to one of the largest hydrangea and azalea gardens in the prefecture, as well as a spectacular panoramic view of the Osaka Plain.

sights.name: Yato Shrine
sights.description: It is an ancient shrine listed in the Engishiki Shinmeicho (list of Shinto shrines) of 927 (5th year of Encho) during the Heian period.

sights.name: Ojoin Rokumanji Temple
sights.description: Since the Heian period, the temple has flourished as a devout temple of Pure Land Buddhism, where people would watch the setting sun and practice Nissokan meditation, vowing to go to paradise. It is also home to the grave of Kusunoki Masatsura, who lived during the Nanboku-cho period.

sights.name: Jikoji Temple
sights.description: This ancient temple in Higashi-Osaka is said to have been built by En no Gyoja after he converted an ogre. It is famous for its door-opening and door-closing ceremonies in spring and autumn, as well as its autumn foliage.

sights.name: Hiraoka Park
sights.description: This park is a place where you can enjoy nature throughout the seasons, including cherry blossoms. There are a variety of slides that take advantage of the terrain, making it fun for everyone from families to hikers.

sights.name: Hiraoka Shrine
sights.description: This ancient shrine is known as Kawachi Province's Ichinomiya. It is said to have been founded three years before Emperor Jimmu ascended to the throne, and is also known as "Moto-Kasuga" as it is the origin of Nara's Kasuga Taisha Shrine.

sights.name: Hyotanyama Inari Shrine
sights.description: One of Japan's three great Inari shrines, the shrine is built on the double-circular burial mound of Hyotanyama Kofun.

sights.name: Mount Ikoma
sights.description: Mount Ikoma, located on the border between Osaka and Nara, stands 642 meters above sea level.

sights.name: Ishikiri-Tsurugiya Shrine
sights.description: Known affectionately as "Ishikiri-san" and "the god of boils," the shrine is famous nationwide for its 100-time pilgrimage, in which visitors walk back and forth between the 100-time stone in front of the main hall and the entrance to the shrine.

sights.name: Hanazono Central Park
sights.description: A comfortable space where you can enjoy seasonal flowers, sports, and art. The area is dotted with facilities such as the children's cultural and sports center "Dream 21" and the Civic Art Center adjacent to Higashiosaka Hanazono Rugby Stadium, making it a place for people to relax and interact.

sights.name: Wakae Castle Ruins
sights.description: Built in the early Muromachi period, the castle ruins are also known as the "phantom castle" and were the center of Kawachi Christianity during the Sengoku period.

sights.name: Wakae Kagami Shrine
sights.description: This ancient shrine in Higashi-Osaka City has records dating back to 854. Known for its blessings of intelligence, health, and safe childbirth, the shrine grounds boast an area of 2,000 tsubo (approximately 6,600 square meters).

sights.name: Nagase Shrine
sights.description: This shrine was founded in 1908 by combining eight local shrines belonging to the local deities of the former village of Nagase. During the autumn festival on October 15th, a float is paraded through the shrine, attracting many visitors.

sights.name: Konoike Shinden Kaisho
sights.description: Built in 1707, Konoike Shinden Kaisho was the base for managing new rice fields for the wealthy Edo period merchant Konoike Zenemon Munetoshi III, and is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan.

sights.name: Forest of Osaka (Nukata park)
sights.description: This natural park boasts one of the largest hydrangea and azalea gardens in the prefecture, as well as a panoramic view of the Osaka Plain. Hiking trails are also available.

sights.name: Dark Pass
sights.description: This pass has been known as the shortest route connecting Osaka and Nara since the Nara period. It is also famous as the place where Matsuo Basho composed his haiku, and during the Edo period it developed as a route for pilgrims to Ise Shrine.

sights.name: Sannomiya Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is famous as a place for praying for rain. Historically, farmers would pray here for rain during droughts, and in return for their prayers being answered, sumo wrestling and Noh/Kyogen performances were offered.

sights.name: Katano Tenjin Shrine
sights.description: Its origins date back to the establishment of a suburban altar by Emperor Kanmu in the 6th year of the Enryaku era (787). The main hall is a nationally designated important cultural property, and within the grounds is Kifune Shrine, which is said to be the site of Emperor Keitai's Kuzuha Palace.

sights.name: Legendary King's Tomb
sights.description: This Osaka Prefecture designated historic site is said to be the tomb of Wani, a scholar from Baekje who is said to have brought the Analects of Confucius and the Thousand Character Classic to Japan.

sights.name: Itsukushima Shrine (Hirakata City)
sights.description: This shrine is located in Hirakata City, Osaka Prefecture. It houses the main hall of Kasuga Shrine, a branch shrine designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan, and displays a valuable architectural style believed to date from the mid to late Muromachi period.

sights.name: Yamadaike Park

sights.name: Dainenji Temple (Ibaraki City)
sights.description: This Jodo sect temple boasts one of the oldest histories in Ibaraki City, Osaka Prefecture, and is associated with Fujiwara no Kamatari. It was founded in the Asuka period by Fujiwara no Kamatari and his eldest son, Joe.

sights.name: Daimonji Temple
sights.description: This Shingon Buddhist temple boasts a history of over 1250 years. Its principal image, Nyoirin Kannon Bodhisattva, and the Four Heavenly Kings are designated as important national cultural properties. It is also famous as a spot for viewing autumn foliage.

sights.name: Higashi Honganji Ibaraki Betsuin
sights.description: This temple belongs to the Otani branch of the Jodo Shinshu sect and is located in Ibaraki City, Osaka Prefecture. Founded in 1603 by Abbot Kyonyo, it boasts a history of 400 years. Highlights include the magnificent temple complex, the largest in Ibaraki City, and the 400-year-old "Kosei Pine."

sights.name: Isora Shrine (also known as Iromizu Shrine)
sights.description: Known since ancient times as "wart water," it is renowned as sacred water with miraculous efficacy in curing not only warts but also various other illnesses. The sacred spring "Tama-no-i" in front of the shrine attracts worshippers seeking to cure warts.

sights.name: Sojiji Temple
sights.description: This famous temple is the 22nd temple of the Thirty-three Kannon Temples of the Western Provinces.

sights.name: Ibaraki City Christian Relics Museum
sights.description: The museum exhibits valuable Christian relics that were passed down in the Senjiji area of Ibaraki City, known as a village of hidden Christians, including the "Statue of St. Francis Xavier (replica)" and "The Fifteen Mysteries of Mary (replica)," which are featured in textbooks.

sights.name: Ibaraki Municipal Kawabata Literature Memorial Hall
sights.description: Kawabata Yasunari, the first Japanese to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, spent his childhood in Ibaraki from the age of three until he graduated from junior high school under the old system.

sights.name: Ibaraki Shrine
sights.description: Located in Ibaraki City, Osaka Prefecture, this is a historic shrine with an inner sanctuary boasting over 1200 years of history, and a main hall that celebrated its 400th anniversary.

activities.name: Kuanji Temple
activities.description: This temple is the 12th sacred site of the Kansai Flower Temples. You can enjoy a variety of flowers and trees throughout the year, including peonies and azaleas in spring, hydrangeas and water lilies in early summer, autumn leaves in fall, and camellias and wintersweets in winter.

activities.name: Satsukiyama Park
activities.description: Spreading from the foot to the middle of Mount Satsuki, the symbol of Ikeda City, this is a famous spot for cherry blossoms, azaleas, and autumn leaves. It is ideal for leisure activities, with the free admission Satsukiyama Zoo and hiking trails offering views of the Osaka Plain.

activities.name: Satsukiyama Zoo
activities.description: Located within Satsukiyama Park in Ikeda City, this zoo is free to enter. It's a leisure spot with a laid-back atmosphere where you can enjoy hiking and picnics.

activities.name: Suigetsu Park
activities.description: Located in Ikeda City, Osaka Prefecture, this park is lush with water and greenery and is known as a famous spot for plum blossoms and irises. It is also famous for the Chinese building "Saiho-tei," which was a gift from Suzhou City, China, a sister city of Ikeda.

sights.name: Cup Noodles Museum Osaka Ikeda
sights.description: This hands-on food education museum teaches you about the history of instant ramen. The hugely popular "My Cup Noodle Factory" allows you to create your own one-of-a-kind original cup noodle.

sights.name: Ichijo-in Temple
sights.description: This temple was rebuilt in 1638 as a sub-temple of Wakaoji Temple, which, although historical records are preserved, was destroyed by fire during the time of Nobunaga. The temple grounds include a large ginkgo tree, the Yuzudo Hall, and the main hall which enshrines the Holy Kannon Bodhisattva.

sights.name: Kureha Shrine
sights.description: This shrine enshrines Gofuku, the first deity of weaving and sewing in Japan. The stained glass at the front of the worship hall is distinctive, and there are many amulets and other items with textile motifs.

sights.name: Ikeda Castle Ruins Park
sights.description: This park was developed on the former site of the castle of the Ikeda clan, a local clan from the Muromachi to Sengoku periods. It features a Japanese garden, an observation rest building, a teahouse, and a view of the city.

sights.name: Hankyu Foundation Itsuo Museum of Art
sights.description: This museum houses and exhibits approximately 5,500 pieces of art and crafts, including old calligraphy, picture scrolls, and ceramics, collected by Ichizo Kobayashi (Itsuo), the founder of Hankyu Railway and Takarazuka Revue.

sights.name: Hankyu Cultural Foundation Ikeda Library
sights.description: This library was founded by Ichizo Kobayashi, a businessman known for his work with Hankyu Railway and the Takarazuka Revue. It houses over 280,000 books related to theater, literature, and the history of Hankyu Railway.

sights.name: Atago Shrine
sights.description: Atago Shrine, located on Satsukiyama in Ikeda City, Osaka Prefecture, has long been worshipped as the god of fire and is known as the base of the Gangara Fire Festival, an intangible cultural property of Osaka Prefecture, which has been held since the Edo period.

sights.name: Kuboso Memorial Museum of Arts

sights.name: Osaka Prefectural Museum of Yayoi Culture
sights.description: Located next to the Ikegami-Sone ruins, this is the only museum in Japan that specializes in Yayoi culture in general.

sights.name: Makiosan Sefukuji Temple

sights.name: Izumi Inoue Shrine

sights.name: Kuzunoha Inari Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is dedicated to the fox associated with the "Kuzunoha Legend." It is known for the legend of the white fox said to be the mother of the Onmyoji (exorcist) Abe no Seimei, and many people visit to pray for children.

sights.name: Inryoji Temple
sights.description: This temple in Izumi City is known for its "blood ceiling," made from old materials from Fushimi Momoyama Castle, and its Osmanthus fragrans, a natural monument designated by Osaka Prefecture.

sights.name: Saifukuji Temple
sights.description: This temple in Izumi City, Osaka Prefecture, is home to the legendary Thunder Well where an old woman is said to have sealed away lightning, and is said to be the origin of the spell "Kuwabara, Kuwabara."

sights.name: Amidaji Temple
sights.description: This temple, located in Izumi City, Osaka Prefecture, is famous for prayers for safe childbirth. It boasts a history of over 1200 years and houses an Amida Buddha statue associated with Empress Komyo.

day_to_day.name: Rinku Premium Outlets Information Center/Welcome Center
day_to_day.description: This tourist information center is located inside the Rinku Premium Outlets, about a six-minute walk from Rinku Town Station. In addition to providing information in Japanese, English, and Chinese, it also has wheelchair rentals and a foreign currency exchange machine.

day_to_day.name: Tourism Hospitality Plaza "Izumisano Machidokoro"
day_to_day.description: This is a tourist information hub for the Izumisano City area, located across from Kansai International Airport. In addition to tourist information, it also offers local product sales, transportation ticket sales, and temporary luggage storage.

day_to_day.name: Tourism Exchange Plaza "Rinku Machidokoro"
day_to_day.description: This is a tourist information center for Izumisano City and Osaka, certified by the Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO). It also sells local products, offers luggage storage, provides foreign currency exchange, and sells various transportation tickets.

day_to_day.name: Kansai International Airport
day_to_day.description: The world's first "offshore airport made of a completely artificial island" was built off the coast of Senshu in Osaka Bay. As a world-class airport that operates 24 hours a day, it connects many cities both in Japan and overseas.

activities.name: e-Stadium Izumisano
activities.description: This e-sports facility is directly connected to Rinku Town Station, one stop away from Kansai Airport Station, and offers free access to professional gaming PCs. Beginners, families, and children can all enjoy themselves with peace of mind.

activities.name: Rinku Pleasure Town SEACLE
activities.description: Located near Kansai International Airport, this amusement facility is fun for the whole family. It features a large Ferris wheel called "Rinku no Hoshi" and a hot spring facility called "Rinku no Yu."

activities.name: Rinku Premium Outlets
activities.description: Located across from Kansai International Airport, this is one of the largest outlet malls in western Japan, where you can enjoy shopping at around 250 stores selling famous domestic and international brands.

activities.name: Exciting Kansai Airport Tour Plan "Exploring the Behind the Scenes at Kansai Airport"
activities.description: This bus tour features an official guide introducing the facilities and work at Kansai International Airport. You can also see security areas that are normally off-limits, such as the in-flight catering factory and the international cargo area, from the bus window.

activities.name: Kitashoji Sake Brewery
activities.description: Founded in 1921, this is the only sake brewery in Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture. They produce local sake, including their flagship brand "Shono Sato," and offer brewery tours, a cafe, and tasting/sales.

activities.name: Izumisano Fisheries Cooperative Open-Air Market
activities.description: The open-air market inside Izumisano Fishing Port sells fresh seafood caught that day. There are also restaurants and sushi shops inside the market, so you can enjoy lively, fresh fish on the spot.

activities.name: Kanku Ice Arena
activities.description: Located in Rinku Town overlooking Kansai Airport, this year-round international standard ice skating rink has seating for up to 1,500 people.

activities.name: Kansai Airport Observation Hall "Sky View"
activities.description: An observation facility where you can enjoy a 360° panoramic view of the runway and passenger terminal building. This is the best vantage point for watching planes take off and land up close. It also houses one of Japan's largest aviation-related shops and a Sky Museum.

activities.name: KIX DUTY FREE, a duty-free shop directly operated by Kansai Airport
activities.description: This is a duty-free shop directly operated by Kansai International Airport. Boasting one of the largest selections in the airport, it offers a wide variety of products including global cosmetics, perfumes, alcohol, tobacco, watches, and souvenirs, including brands making their debut in Japan.

sights.name: Rinku Town
sights.description: Located across the water from Kansai International Airport, known as the "gateway to the world," this international city is a popular tourist spot in southern Osaka, where shopping, accommodation, gourmet food, parks, beaches and more are all gathered together.

sights.name: Rinku Park
sights.description: This park has an excellent location, overlooking planes taking off from Kansai International Airport and Awaji Island and the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge in the distance. The sunset from Marble Beach, which has been selected as one of the top 100 sunsets in Japan, is a must-see.

sights.name: Oiseki Park
sights.description: Located in Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture, this park is one of the "100 Best Green Spots in Osaka." It is a naturally rich park known for the clear streams and strange rock formations of the Roji Valley, and for its cherry blossoms, Somei Yoshino, which bloom in the spring.

sights.name: Nakami Shrine
sights.description: Located in Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture, this shrine was founded in the late Heian period.

sights.name: okami Shrine (Izumisano City)
sights.description: Located in Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture, this shrine enshrines Takaokami, the goddess of rain. The main hall, built in 1442, is the oldest Kasuga-style building in Osaka Prefecture and is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan.

sights.name: Jigen-in Temple
sights.description: This is the oldest temple in Senshu, built at the request of Emperor Tenmu. The pagoda, built during the Kamakura period, is designated as a national treasure.

sights.name: Hinone Shrine
sights.description: Hine Shrine, located in Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture, is a historic shrine known for its annual festival, the "Makura Matsuri," held in May.

sights.name: Hibashiri Shrine
sights.description: The enshrined deity is Kagutsuchi-no-kami, who is said to be the god who controls fire and water.

sights.name: Mount Inunaki
sights.description: Mount Inunaki is known as a sacred place where Japan's oldest Shugendo training center, Shipporyu-ji Temple, is located, and is also known as the Women's Omine.

sights.name: Inunakiyama Shippo-ryuji Temple
sights.description: Founded in 661 (the 7th year of the reign of Empress Saimei), this is the head temple of the Inunaki school of Shingon Buddhism. The principal image is Kurikara Dairyu Acala, known as the guardian deity of wish fulfillment and the protector of good fortune.

sights.name: Arito Shrine
sights.description: This ancient shrine in Izumisano City, Osaka Prefecture, is deeply connected to the history and culture of the Heian period poet Ki no Tsurayuki, the legend of the shrine's name in "The Pillow Book," and the Noh play "Ant Pass" by Zeami. It also hosts Noh performances.

sights.name: Former Mukai Family Residence
sights.description: This thatched-roof farmhouse is a well-preserved example of Edo-period architecture in the Sennan region. Believed to have been built around 1802 (Kyowa 2), it features distinctive architectural techniques such as a staggered four-room layout and high ceilings.

sights.name: Nishikinohama Park Seaside Green Space
sights.description: This seaside spot offers a variety of activities, including barbecues and jet skiing. You can also enjoy board sailing and jet skiing at the jet sports facility.

sights.name: Nishikinohama Beach
sights.description: This Osaka beach is impressive for its beautiful green pine groves and white sand. You can enjoy clam digging from early April to early June, and swimming from mid-July to late August.

sights.name: Nishikinohama Shellfish Digging Area
sights.description: Nishikinohama Beach Kaizuka City is a spacious beach stretching for about 1km, a 10-minute walk from Nishikinohama Station on the Nankai Main Line. Clam digging is permitted every year between April and June, and the beach is bustling with families.

sights.name: Osaka Prefectural Nishikinohama Park
sights.description: The park's symbolic sailing ship mast monument stands out against the blue sky, and Nishiki Beach, with its white sand and pleasant sea breeze, is the closest swimming beach to central Kansai.

sights.name: Kanden Shrine
sights.description: Located in Kaizuka City, Osaka Prefecture, this shrine is the tutelary deity (guardian deity of the land) of Kaizuka Jinanimachi. Formerly known as Kanda Kawara Daimyojin, it is a shrine with a rich historical background.

sights.name: Mizumadera Temple
sights.description: This ancient temple is said to have been founded by Gyoki at the request of Emperor Shomu in 744. It is deeply revered as a Kannon statue that wards off evil spirits, and is the fourth temple on the New Saigoku Pilgrimage.

sights.name: Wakihama Ebisu Taisha Shrine (Takaokami Shrine)
sights.description: Along with Imamiya Ebisu and Nishinomiya Ebisu, it is known as one of the three major Ebisu shrines and is the oldest Ebisu shrine in Senshu.

sights.description: This historic temple, which is also the origin of the place name Gantaobata, belongs to the Shinshu Otani sect and enshrines Amida Buddha as its principal image.

sights.name: Tsuboi-dera Temple

sights.name: Toothpick Reference Room
sights.description: This unique exhibition facility allows visitors to learn about the differences, history, and manufacturing methods of toothpicks from Japan and around the world.

sights.name: Osaka Prefectural Flower Garden
sights.description: The park boasts an area three times larger than Koshien Stadium, and visitors can enjoy seasonal flowers in decorative flower beds, rose gardens, hydrangea gardens, etc.

sights.name: Tenjin Shrine
sights.description: Located in Kawachinagano City, Osaka Prefecture, this shrine is known as the guardian deity of the seven villages of Takihata.

sights.name: Iwawaki Temple
sights.description: This sacred site of Katsuragi Shugendo is located on the mountainside of Mt. Iwawaki (500m above sea level). It houses the Tahoto Pagoda, an important cultural property, and a seated statue of Vairocana Buddha from the late Heian period.

sights.name: Takihata Falls
sights.description: This scenic spot is located in the mountains of Kawachinagano City, near the border with Wakayama Prefecture. Home to numerous waterfalls, including Otaki, Gokotaki, and Gongentaki, it is popular as a hiking trail and outdoor spot.

sights.name: Takihata Hometown Cultural Heritage Forest Center
sights.description: The museum preserves and exhibits many cultural assets, including folklore, arts and crafts, and traditional houses, from the Takihata area, which was to be submerged by the construction of the Takihata Dam.

sights.name: Takihata Dam
sights.description: The affectionate "Mandarin Ducks of Takihata Dam" is one of the Eight Views of Shinkawachinagano. Enjoy a stroll around the lush dam lake. This multipurpose dam was completed in 1982, and the surrounding area is equipped with a campground, walking trails, fishing ponds, and more.

sights.name: Yakujusan Enmeiji Temple
sights.description: Founded during the Konin era (Heian period), this temple is known for its 1,000-year-old "Sunset Maple Tree," a natural monument designated by Osaka Prefecture.

sights.name: Kanshinji Temple
sights.description: Located on the border of Osaka, Nara, and Wakayama prefectures, Kanshinji Temple is an ancient temple of the Koyasan Shingon sect that was founded by En no Gyoja and rebuilt by Kukai (Kobo Daishi).

sights.name: Nagano Park
sights.description: Comprised of five areas (Nagano, Kawai-ji, Kanshin-ji/Maruyama, Enmei-ji, and Amano-san) scattered at the foot of the Kongo Mountains, this park is rich in nature and allows visitors to experience the changing seasons. It is known as a famous spot for cherry blossoms and autumn leaves.

sights.name: Mount Iwawaki
sights.description: Located in Kawachinagano City, Osaka Prefecture, this 897.7m high mountain is covered in beautiful waves of Japanese pampas grass on its summit. The autumn "Japanese pampas grass" is a spectacular sight, and the mountain trails are well maintained, making it a popular hiking course.

stays.name: Campground in Kawachinagano
stays.name_ja: 光滝寺キャンプ場
stays.description: This lush green campsite is conveniently located about 1 hour and 30 minutes by car from downtown Osaka and about 30 minutes from downtown Kawachinagano. Located upstream from Takihata Dam, you can enjoy hiking to the scenic spot "Hikaritaki," auto camping, and fishing.

stays.description: This hot spring inn boasts a historic natural hot spring that is said to have been gushing out since the time of Empress Suiko, and seasonal kaiseki cuisine. Located about 30 minutes from Osaka city, it is easily accessible, and you can enjoy overnight stays, day trips to the baths, and meals.

sights.name: Kishiwada Nature Museum
sights.description: The facility introduces the nature of southern Osaka, centered around Kishiwada, through a variety of specimens and dioramas.

sights.name: Fugu Museum
sights.description: The museum displays numerous items related to pufferfish, including skeletal specimens and folk art. Founded in 1964 by Kiichi Kitahama, it boasts a collection of 2,500 items related to pufferfish.

sights.name: Gofusou
sights.description: The former site of the new teahouse of the Okabe clan, the former lord of Kishiwada Castle, is a mansion built over a period of 10 years, and a beautiful strolling garden with a teahouse and snow-viewing lanterns.

sights.name: Kitasaka Town Tourist Farm
sights.description: This tourist farm in Kishiwada City offers a panoramic view of Osaka Bay. You can experience mandarin orange picking and sweet potato digging, and after picking you can even enjoy sukiyaki. This is a spot where both adults and children can enjoy a day in nature.

sights.name: Tenshoji Temple (Octopus Jizo)
sights.description: This temple is known for the legend that an octopus and a white monk (Jizo Bodhisattva) saved Kishiwada Castle from falling. The Jizo Bodhisattva is enshrined in one of Japan's largest Jizo halls.

sights.name: Kishiwada Castle
sights.description: Kishiwada Castle served as the southern defense for Osaka Castle during the Edo period. The current castle tower was rebuilt in 1954, and in addition to being able to enjoy document exhibits and a watchtower, the "Hachijin Garden" designed by Mirei Shigemori is also a must-see.

sights.name: Kishijo Shrine
sights.description: Located east of the Kishiwada Castle keep, this shrine is the guardian deity of the castle and a sacred site for the Kishiwada Danjiri Festival. It is widely worshipped as the god of matchmaking.

sights.name: Sengoji Temple
sights.description: This is the family temple of the Okabe family, lords of Kishiwada Castle in Izumi Province. It originated as a temple in the retirement residence of Okabe Minokami Yoshikatsu, the first lord of Kishiwada Castle, and has served as the family temple for successive generations of the Okabe family.

sights.name: Tsumikawa Shrine
sights.description: Tsumikawa Shrine, one of the five shrines of Izumi Province, was founded during the reign of Emperor Sujin. Prayers for rain were offered here during a severe drought, and the main hall, rebuilt by Toyotomi Hideyori, is a designated Important Cultural Property of Japan.

sights.name: Tomboike Park
sights.description: Located in Kishiwada City, Osaka Prefecture, this vast park is approximately the size of 16.5 Koshien Stadiums. You can enjoy seasonal flowers such as roses, hydrangeas, and daffodils, as well as large playground equipment with dragonfly and butterfly motifs, and a long slide.

sights.name: Kishiwada Danjiri Kaikan
sights.description: This museum allows visitors to experience the history and excitement of the Kishiwada Danjiri Festival, which boasts a 300-year tradition, through actual exhibits and the latest video technology.

sights.name: Keihan Electric Railway Co., Ltd. Neyagawa Rolling Stock Factory
sights.description: This exhibit introduces the equipment used in the inspection and maintenance of railway vehicles. By observing how vehicles are inspected and maintained, visitors can think about the safety and convenience of railways.

sights.name: Ninnaji Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is located in Neyagawa City, Osaka Prefecture. The name of the place comes from the fact that it was once the territory of Ninna-ji Temple in Kyoto. It is said to have been founded in the early Muromachi period and is also known as Tenmangu Shrine, which enshrines Sugawara no Michizane.

sights.name: Kanda Tenmangu Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is located in Neyagawa City, Osaka Prefecture. It is famous for its hanging scroll of Sugawara no Michizane, whose face is said to turn red when offerings of sacred sake, and for its large camphor tree (a natural monument-class tree) that is over 800 years old.

sights.name: Kayashima Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is famous for its gigantic camphor tree (O-kusu), which towers over the platform of Kayashima Station on the Keihan Main Line. It has also been selected as one of Osaka Prefecture's 100 Best Green Spaces.
