day_to_day.name: Tourist Information OSAKA
day_to_day.description: This tourist information center is located in front of the central ticket gates of JR Osaka Station, one of Japan's leading terminal stations. It offers multilingual support (English, Chinese, and Korean) and also houses a JR railway information center and a travel service center.

day_to_day.name: Tourist Information NAMBA
day_to_day.description: This tourist information center is located on the first floor of Nankai Namba Station, which is easily accessible from Kansai International Airport. It provides tourist information for the popular Minami area of Osaka.

day_to_day.name: Yodoyabashi Tourist Information Center
day_to_day.description: This convenient tourist information center is located next to Yodoyabashi Station on the Keihan Railway and Osaka Metro Midosuji Line. It provides multilingual information on Osaka's History / culture, as well as tourist spots in Kyoto, Shiga, and other areas.

day_to_day.name: DOTON PLAZA
day_to_day.description: A commercial facility that sells a variety of items, including miscellaneous goods, daily necessities, watches, and precious metals. It also has a tourist information center that provides service in English, Chinese, and Korean.

day_to_day.name: Pivot BASE Travel Cafe @ Tonbori
day_to_day.description: A tourist exchange hub (cafe and pub) that digitally showcases local information rooted in the region and allows locals and tourists to enjoy interacting with each other.

day_to_day.name: ROAD BIKE RENTAL JAPAN
day_to_day.description: We are a specialty shop offering bicycle rentals, cycling tours, and cycling packages. Professional cyclists support your cycling experience throughout Japan, primarily in Osaka and Kyoto.

day_to_day.name: TKTS Tourist Information NAMBA
day_to_day.description: Originally from Broadway in New York, this ticket booth offers discounted tickets to today's and tomorrow's entertainment, including musicals, plays, kabuki, bunraku, music, and sports.

day_to_day.name: WILLER Bus Terminal Osaka Umeda
day_to_day.description: This large bus terminal is located on the first floor of Osaka's landmark, Umeda Sky Building. As a tourist information hub, it is equipped with facilities such as free Wi-Fi, power outlets, coin lockers, and powder rooms.

day_to_day.name: Umeda International Clinic
day_to_day.description: This clinic welcomes a wide range of people, including foreign tourists visiting Japan, who are experiencing health problems during their stay in Osaka. We offer services in English, Chinese, and Korean, and also accept consultations via WhatsApp.

day_to_day.name: Ee-an Osaka Tourist Information Cafe
day_to_day.description: This tourist information center is located right next to Nipponbashi Station in Osaka. It offers local Osaka information not found in guidebooks, luggage storage, reservation services, bicycle rentals, pocket Wi-Fi rentals, sightseeing tours, and more. There is also a cafe on-site.

day_to_day.name: Kirindo Pharmacy (4th floor, Herbis Osaka)
day_to_day.description: Located next to a clinic with various medical departments, this pharmacy can handle medications for a wide range of symptoms. In addition to prescription medications, they also stock over-the-counter drugs. English-speaking staff are also available.

day_to_day.name: Don Quijote Dotonbori store
day_to_day.description: One of Japan's largest discount stores, it is marked by the yellow Ferris wheel, a landmark of Osaka Minami. It has a 24-hour tourist information center and a duty-free counter, and offers multilingual support.

day_to_day.name: Don Quijote Dotonbori Midosuji Store
day_to_day.description: This information center is located inside a large Don Quijote store facing Midosuji in Dotonbori. It is open 24 hours a day and offers convenient services for foreign visitors to Japan, including multilingual support and a duty-free counter.

day_to_day.name: Volunteer Tourist Guides
day_to_day.description: Members of the Osaka Tourist Volunteer Guide Association will convey the charm and excitement of Osaka through free introductions to its history, culture, and tourist attractions.

day_to_day.name: Tourist Information SHIN-OSAKA
day_to_day.description: This tourist information center is located on the 3rd floor concourse of JR Shin-Osaka Station. It provides tourist information about Osaka, sells tourist tickets, and provides multilingual support.

day_to_day.name: Shin-Umeda City General Information Center
day_to_day.description: This is the general information center for Shin-Umeda City, where the Umeda Sky Building (Floating Garden Observatory) is located. In addition to providing information about the facility, they also offer advice on sightseeing in Osaka.

day_to_day.name: Nipponbashi General Information Center
day_to_day.description: Tourist information center located at Nipponbashi (Denden Town) in Osaka, providing multilingual maps with information on over 500 stores, baggage storage, foreign currency exchange, and other services.

day_to_day.name: Abeno Harukas Kintetsu Main Store Foreign Customer's Salon
day_to_day.description: We provide a variety of services to foreign tourists visiting Japan, including tax exemption procedures, distribution of 5% discount coupons, overseas delivery, tourist information, foreign currency exchange, ATMs, and more.

day_to_day.name: Hankyu Tourist Center, Umeda, Osaka
day_to_day.description: This tourist information center is operated by Hankyu Railway, which connects Osaka with Kobe, Takarazuka, and Kyoto. They offer tourist and transportation information, ticket sales, Wi-Fi router rentals, and kimono photo shoot locations.

activities.name: Universal Studios Japan
activities.description: A series of super moving and super exciting experiences that will leave you feeling more energized than anywhere else!

activities.name: Tempozan Ferris Wheel
activities.description: With a diameter of 100m, this Ferris wheel is one of the largest in the world and offers a 15-minute flight. The beautiful lighting is like a fireworks display.

activities.name: Kuromon Market
activities.description: Known as "Osaka's kitchen" and "Osaka's stomach," this 580m-long shopping arcade is lined with around 150 stores, mainly fresh fishmongers, and is popular with both domestic and international tourists for its gourmet food and snacks, including sushi, seafood bowls, and grilled skewers.

activities.name: Namba Parks
activities.description: This huge complex opened on the site of the former Osaka Baseball Stadium. It is an urban oasis with a shopping zone, restaurants, one of the largest cinema complexes in Osaka, and a rooftop garden called Parks Garden where you can enjoy 100,000 flowers of approximately 500 different species.

activities.name: Grand Front Osaka
activities.description: Grand Front Osaka on the north side of Osaka Station has 266 shops and restaurants.

activities.name: Kyocera Dome Osaka
activities.description: As the home stadium of the Orix Buffaloes, this multi-dome can accommodate baseball games, concerts, and various other events. Dome tours are also available, allowing you to explore behind the scenes of the stadium.

activities.name: Tempozan Marketplace
activities.description: A large commercial facility adjacent to the Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan. It is a tourist hub for the Osaka Bay area, with a variety of attractions including Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokocho, where you can find a variety of Naniwa foods, around 80 unique shops, and an indoor zoo.

activities.name: Osaka Duck Tours
activities.description: A first in Japan! A new way to enjoy the view of Osaka city from both land and water. An attraction unique to the hugely popular water metropolis of Osaka!

activities.name: Billboard Live OSAKA
activities.description: Billboard, a music brand with over 100 years of history, originated in the United States as an entertainment magazine, operates this live music venue. You can enjoy high-quality performances by top domestic and international artists, along with cuisine prepared by a first-class chef.

activities.name: Zepp Namba
activities.description: This multipurpose live hall can be used for music, plays, lectures, exhibitions, and more. Equipped with the latest lighting and sound equipment, you can enjoy the best sound no matter where you are in the seating.

activities.name: ALLYS Umeda
activities.description: Get stunningly cute with Korean hair styling and Illumina color in Umeda/Chaya. We offer exceptional service with meticulous techniques and hospitality that leverage the unique strengths of each staff member.

activities.name: ATC Hall
activities.description: Located in the Osaka Bay area, this multipurpose hall consists of five halls. It can flexibly accommodate all kinds of events, including seminars and training sessions, and can also accommodate bonded exhibitions.

activities.name: Amazing Kart ISK Osaka Maishima store
activities.description: Come empty-handed and with no driver's license required, this is a full-scale go-kart circuit where you can experience what it's like to be an F1 racer.

activities.name: Asue Arena Osaka (Osaka Municipal Central Gymnasium)
activities.description: This is a multi-purpose space that is semi-underground, a rare sight worldwide, with all facilities located underground, including the main arena, sub-arena, judo hall, kendo hall, and large, medium and small conference rooms.

activities.name: Asue Osaka Pool
activities.description: This sports facility can be used as a 50m swimming pool and diving pool in the summer, and as an ice skating rink in the winter. The 25m sub-pool is open all year round.

activities.name: BLANZ Shinsaibashi
activities.description: We offer photo shoots using 30 studio sets, one of the largest in the Kansai region, and at famous Osaka landmarks. We have a wide selection of both traditional Japanese attire and Western-style dresses, and your shoot will be handled by a popular photographer.

activities.name: EST
activities.description: This shopping street located under the elevated railway in Umeda, Osaka, targets women in their late teens to early twenties. It's packed with the latest fashion, cafes, and Japanese restaurants.

activities.name: Gardener's Tenshiba i:na store
activities.description: Local business in Tennoji Ward, Osaka.

activities.name: HACOSTADIUM Osaka
activities.description: One of Japan's largest cosplay photo studios, with over 35 different types of professional photo shoot spaces. It's a cosplay amusement space where you can enjoy photo shoots all day long in a variety of backgrounds, including a school, a Japanese-style room, and ruins.

activities.name: HEP FIVE
activities.description: Located in Umeda, Osaka, this commercial complex is symbolized by a 75m diameter red Ferris wheel and a giant whale in the atrium. It is packed with the latest fashion, anime goods, collaboration cafes, and more.

activities.name: HEP FIVE FERRIS WHEEL
activities.description: This bright red Ferris wheel is located in the heart of Umeda, Osaka. With a diameter of 75m and a maximum height of 106m above ground, it offers a spectacular view from central Osaka all the way to the Akashi Strait.

activities.name: HERBIS PLAZA/PLAZA ENT
activities.description: A large-scale complex in Nishi-Umeda, in front of JR Osaka Station, that includes first-class brand stores, select shops, restaurants, a hotel, a hall, and more.

activities.name: Hoop
activities.description: A commercial facility in Tennoji, Osaka, that brings together famous fashion brands, unique select shops, large specialty stores, and restaurants.

activities.name: JO-TERRACE OSAKA
activities.description: The new entrance to Osaka Castle Park is a facility with restaurants, cafes, and shops in a relaxing, modern Japanese space.

activities.name: JUMP SHOP Osaka Shinsaibashi store
activities.description: This is an official Shueisha licensed shop filled with original illustration goods, mainly featuring popular works currently serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump, such as "ONE PIECE," "My Hero Academia," and "Jujutsu Kaisen."

activities.name: Joshin SUPER KIDS LAND Main Store
activities.description: One of Japan's largest specialty stores, the entire building is filled with hobbies! Gunpla, model trains, Tamiya products, radio-controlled cars, air guns, and more are all available on each floor.

activities.name: Joshin Super Kids Land Main Store
activities.description: One of Japan's largest specialty model shops. From the first to fifth floors, the shop is packed with a wide variety of hobbies, including Gundam plastic models, figurines, characters, model trains, and dollhouses.

activities.name: KPG RIVER CRUISE Osaka Houseboat
activities.description: This cruise service allows you to enjoy banquets while boarding a boat and viewing the rivers of Osaka, the water city. From authentic kaiseki cuisine to Italian and BBQ, you can enjoy the scenery of the four seasons.

activities.name: LUCUA Osaka
activities.description: Consisting of the East Building "LUCUA" and the West Building "LUCUA 1100," this is one of the largest fashion buildings in Japan, directly connected to Osaka Station and home to approximately 500 stores. It offers a wide range of shopping, restaurants, and sweet shops.

activities.name: Namba Nannan
activities.description: NAMBA Nan Nan in Minami is known as the pioneer of underground shopping malls in Osaka.

activities.name: NU Chayamachi/NU Chayamachi PLUS
activities.description: This new, cutting-edge spot in Kita, Osaka, offers a lifestyle for adults. It houses around 100 stores, including fashion, lifestyle, music stores, and CD shops.

activities.name: Ninja-Do
activities.description: Located close to Shin-Imamiya Station and Dobutsuen-mae Station, this facility allows you to change into authentic ninja costumes and experience ninja walking, sword stances, blowguns, shuriken, and more. VR experiences and local walking options are also available.

activities.name: OAP (Osaka Amenity Park)
activities.description: Located on the banks of the Okawa River that flows through Osaka, the city of water, this complex comprises the OAP Tower & Plaza, Imperial Hotel Osaka, a gallery, apartments, and a park.

activities.name: OMM
activities.description: Located in Tenmabashi, Osaka, this comprehensive building is a business information hub with 11 large and small halls, as well as nine large and small conference rooms that can accommodate 12 to 500 people, and a gallery.

activities.name: HASHI LAB Shinsaibashi
activities.description: Experience Japanese culture through tea ceremony, calligraphy, and silk cocoon flower arranging in the historic space of the Osaka Norin Kaikan.

activities.name: Samurai and Ninja Experience
activities.description: Experience authentic samurai and ninja action! This is an interactive tourist spot where you can learn the action of "sword fighting" used on stage and in movies under the guidance of an instructor.

activities.name: Sushi Making Experience Namba
activities.description: It features an experience of making 12 pieces of sushi, the opportunity to wear a sushi chef's uniform, English guidance, and accommodating a variety of dietary restrictions (vegetarian, vegan, halal).

activities.name: TMT OSAKA
activities.description: The designs incorporate the subcultures of the good old days of America from the 1900s to the 1970s into each item from a unique perspective. This is the only directly managed store in the Kansai region that offers items that are committed to being MADE IN JAPAN/REAL VINTAGE.

activities.name: TUGBOAT_TAISHO (Tugboat Taisho)
activities.description: Located on the waterfront of the Shirinashi River in Taisho Ward, Osaka City, this complex brings together food, music, art, and crafts. With a focus on unique food, you can also enjoy events and live performances.

activities.name: The Kitahama Plaza
activities.description: A commercial facility with a collection of high-quality, unique stores, befitting Kita-Senba, a town with many historic buildings.

activities.name: Washoku Home Cooking - Machiko -
activities.description: A completely private cooking class where you can learn Japanese home cooking and dining etiquette at the instructor's home in the heart of Osaka. Vegetarian, vegan, and halal options are available.

activities.name: and
activities.description: An urban commercial complex that supports fashion and comfort in all aspects of life, from daily necessities and fashion to hobbies, learning, and beauty.

activities.name: namBa HIPS
activities.description: A complex leisure facility in the Landmark Tower in the heart of Namba, offering golf, a spa, amusement and dining.

activities.name: Aioi Nissay Dowa Insurance The Phoenix Hall
activities.description: With a total of 335 seats, this "small but sparkling" concert hall plans and organizes unique programs, mainly focusing on classical music.

activities.name: Abeno Q’s Mall
activities.description: This shopping mall in Abeno Ward, Osaka City, is one of the largest in Osaka Prefecture, with 254 stores. It is home to a diverse range of tenants, including SHIBUYA109 ABENO, Ito-Yokado, Hands, and Uniqlo.

activities.name: Abeno Lucius
activities.description: Located in Abeno, Osaka, this multi-purpose building combines a shopping mall, a cultural school, and office space.

activities.name: Amidaike Daikoku: Awaokoshi and Iwaokoshi
activities.description: This long-established company was founded in Bunka 2 (1805) and manufactures and sells "Awa Okoshi," a snack with the longest history in Osaka.

activities.name: Maishima Arena
activities.description: This indoor stadium is located within Maishima Sports Island in Konohana Ward, Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture. It is the home arena of the Osaka Evessa, a professional basketball team in the B.League.

activities.name: Kimono Rental Wargo Osaka Shinsaibashi Store
activities.description: Just a 4-minute walk from the popular tourist spot Dotonbori, Kimono Rental Wargo Osaka Shinsaibashi offers an easily accessible kimono rental experience! Kimono and yukata rentals include free dressing and a complete set of accessories!

activities.name: Kin'ei Apollo Building
activities.description: This complex offers shopping, gourmet food, entertainment, and even a movie theater. It is connected to the neighboring Abeno Lucias and houses large movie theaters such as Abeno Apollo Cinema.

activities.name: Senba Shinsaibashisuji Shopping Street
activities.description: Located on the east side of Osaka's main street, Midosuji, this historic shopping arcade boasts vestiges of its history as a textile wholesale district, great bargains, and a wide variety of gourmet food.

activities.name: Senba Center Building
activities.description: This huge shopping complex stretches about 1km from east to west and is built under the Hanshin Expressway. It houses about 800 wholesale and retail stores selling textiles, shoes, watches, jewelry, and more, as well as restaurants.

activities.name: Naniwa Taiko Studio (Taikosho Co., Ltd.)
activities.description: This is a taiko workshop in Naniwa, Osaka, that has inherited a tradition that dates back hundreds of years. You can enjoy observing the manufacturing process, making your own taiko drum, and even experiencing playing one.

activities.name: Naniwa Specialty Ichibirian Dotonbori Branch
activities.description: The store also houses the official Kuidare Taro shop, "Kuidare Taro Honpo," and is a specialty store stocking 4,000 types of Osaka souvenirs.

activities.name: Namba CITY
activities.description: This vast shopping mall stretches from the second basement floor to the second floor above ground in the Nankai Electric Railway Namba Station terminal building. It houses around 250 stores, including popular brands, trendy item shops, restaurants, and cafes.

activities.name: Namba Hatch
activities.description: A live music venue in Namba, Osaka where you can enjoy live music of various genres, from rock to jazz, soul and hip hop.

activities.name: Namba Walk
activities.description: This underground shopping mall, representing Osaka Minami, is home to around 200 stores selling fashion, gourmet food, miscellaneous goods, cafes, and more. It is a shopping street that runs from Namba Station on Osaka Metro Midosuji Line to Nipponbashi Station.

activities.name: Namba Parks Cinema
activities.description: Shochiku films are screened in 11 theaters. Specially designed screens and cutting-edge sound systems are installed to create a powerful and impressive experience. This movie theater boasts the largest floor area in Osaka Prefecture.

activities.name: O1O1 NAMBA MARUI
activities.description: Marui is always creating the latest fashion trends for young people! You can enjoy the latest entertainment, food, cosmetics, experiences, and services all day long.

activities.name: ATC (Asia-Pacific Trade Center)
activities.description: Located in the bay area of Osaka's Nanko Port, this large-scale commercial complex houses shopping, restaurants, offices, an event hall, and a housing-related exhibition center.

activities.name: Abeno Raku Bus
activities.description: Located in Abeno Harukas Kintetsu Main Store, this is an event and experience space centered around pop culture such as anime and manga.

activities.name: Alde Shin-Osaka
activities.description: A shopping center on the second floor of Shin-Osaka Station, the access point to Kansai. It offers gourmet food, fashion, souvenirs, and more.

activities.name: Illustration and Manga Class egaco Osaka School
activities.description: Located in a commercial facility directly connected to Namba Station, this is a classroom where you can learn how to draw illustrations and manga through individual instruction.Trial lessons are also available, and both individuals and groups can participate.

activities.name: Intex Osaka
activities.description: With a total exhibition area of 70,000 m2, it is the largest exhibition hall in western Japan and hosts a variety of events, including international trade fairs, exhibitions, conferences, seminars, and parties.

activities.name: Edion Arena Osaka (Osaka Prefectural Gymnasium)
activities.description: This multi-purpose sports facility has stadiums and dojos for various sports, including volleyball, basketball, judo, gymnastics, and boxing, as well as a multi-purpose hall and meeting rooms.

activities.name: Compli South Shinsaibashi store
activities.description: We are a comprehensive printing and copying shop where you can consult in person for business cards, posters, flyers, signs, T-shirts, tapestries, novelty goods production, bookbinding, scanning, and more.

activities.name: Captain Line
activities.description: This shuttle boat connects the two major attractions in Osaka Port, Kaiyukan and Universal Studios Japan (USJ), in as little as 10 minutes. It's convenient for sightseeing in the bay area and also allows you to enjoy a mini cruise.

activities.name: Kirara Kujo Shopping Street
activities.description: Located in Nishi-ku, Osaka, this shopping street is approximately 600 meters long and is lined with approximately 150 stores, giving it a traditional downtown atmosphere. It is close to Kyocera Dome Osaka and offers special deals on professional baseball game days.

activities.name: CRYSTA Nagahori
activities.description: Located in Shinsaibashi, the center of Osaka, this is one of Japan's largest underground shopping malls, with around 100 stores selling fashion, miscellaneous goods, and gourmet food.

activities.name: Grand Front Osaka Shops & Restaurants
activities.description: Located in front of Osaka Umeda Station, the largest terminal in western Japan, is the largest shopping town in Japan, with approximately 260 stores ranging from fashion to miscellaneous goods and restaurants.

activities.name: Kokumin Drug Shinsaibashisuji 1-chome store
activities.description: A drugstore with a wide selection of cosmetics from brands such as SK-II, Cle de Peau Beaute, and Shiseido. Foreign language-speaking staff are always available.

activities.name: The Symphony Hall
activities.description: Built in 1982 as Japan's first hall dedicated to classical concerts, it features an acoustic design that boasts a reverberation time of 2 seconds (when fully occupied) and an arena theater format in which all seating surrounds the stage.

activities.name: Ghibli-filled Donguri Republic Namba store
activities.description: We have a wide selection of character goods from Studio Ghibli films, including "My Neighbor Totoro," "Kiki's Delivery Service," and "Spirited Away." The interior of the store is filled with the warmth of wood, creating a relaxing space.

activities.name: Jungle Osaka Nipponbashi store
activities.description: This hobby shop is located on Sakaisuji-dori Nipponbashi Osaka. It stocks a wide variety of products, both old and new, from the latest anime figures to special effects items, super alloy robots, Gunpla, and retro toys.

activities.name: Janjan Yokocho
activities.description: Nanyo-dori Shopping Street, stretching approximately 180 meters north to south, is located in a corner of Shinsekai at the foot of Tsutenkaku Tower. Named after the sound of postwar barkers, it is one of Osaka's leading gourmet spots, lined with kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) and standing bars.

activities.name: SPOTAKA Shinsaibashi Big Step Main Store
activities.description: Located in the heart of America-mura, this comprehensive sports shop stocks all kinds of sports items, from trendy sports like skateboarding, snowboarding, and surfing to sneakers, soccer, and baseball.

activities.name: Suitcase Repair King Shin-Osaka Store
activities.description: Suitcase Repair King is a nationwide suitcase repair specialist. We provide same-day service for problems that occur while traveling or on business trips.

activities.name: Diamor Osaka
activities.description: This bright and open underground shopping mall in Umeda, Osaka, is designed with an Italian streetscape as its motif. It is lined with stores selling apparel, miscellaneous goods, cosmetics, and more.

activities.name: Taekwondo Experience
activities.description: This Osaka taekwondo school was founded by Sydney Olympic medalist Yoriko Okamoto. Everyone from children to seniors can experience taekwondo, which combines the spirit of martial arts with the appeal of sport.

activities.name: Dojima Underground Center
activities.description: Shopping complex in Kita Ward, Osaka.

activities.name: Hilton Plaza East/West
activities.description: This shopping complex in Nishi-Umeda, Osaka, is home to a collection of popular brands from around the world. In addition to shops such as Louis Vuitton, it also has restaurants, general merchandise stores, and rental conference rooms.

activities.name: Bijou Opera Shinsaibashi Studio
activities.description: This accessory workshop in Shinsaibashi, Osaka, allows you to experience making matching rings and bangles. You can take them home on the same day, and there is a wide selection of materials available, from silver to platinum and 18k gold.

activities.name: Bic Camera
activities.description: Located in Sennichimae in Minami, just a short distance from Namba Station in Osaka, this is a large specialty store where many customers from overseas come to shop duty free.

activities.name: Festival Hall
activities.description: Located in Nakanoshima, Osaka, Festival Hall is one of the world's leading music halls, hosting performances of a wide variety of genres, from classical, opera, and ballet to pop, Noh, and Kyogen. It boasts superb acoustics that have been praised as allowing sounds to "rain down from the heavens."

activities.name: Brand Shop Street
activities.description: Around the intersection of Midosuji, which runs north to south through the center of Osaka city, and Nagahori-dori, which runs east to west, is an area lined with world-famous luxury brands such as Chanel, Cartier, Louis Vuitton, and Christian Dior.

activities.name: Whity Umeda
activities.description: Located in the huge terminal of Osaka's Kita area, this huge underground shopping mall has around 300,000 passersby per day. It is lined with around 180 stores, mainly restaurants, but also clothing stores, general goods stores, and bars.

activities.name: Suminoe Boat Race
activities.description: Known as a mecca for boat racing, it is the venue for many major races out of the 24 racecourses in Japan. You can enjoy the unique sense of speed and thrill of the races, as well as the extraordinary experience of night races.

activities.name: Yamada Denki LABI1 Namba
activities.description: This theme park is one of the largest in Japan, boasting an area of approximately 20,000 tsubo (approximately 19,000 m2) and a selection of approximately 800,000 items, from popular home appliances to books and toys.

activities.name: Yanmar Stadium Nagai
activities.description: This is a Type 1 certified athletics stadium by the Japan Association of Athletics Federations. It has a 400m x 9 lane track and a beautiful 107m x 71m natural grass field, and can accommodate approximately 50,000 spectators.

activities.name: Yodobashi Umeda Tower
activities.description: This large commercial complex is the symbol of Osaka Station and is made up of Yodobashi Camera, LINKS UMEDA with around 200 stores, Hotel Hankyu Respire Osaka, and the Oishiimono Yokocho restaurant district.

activities.name: Isshinji Theater Club
activities.description: A multi-purpose hall used for various events, primarily for performing arts, including lectures and workshops.

activities.name: Japan Tate-do Association "Samurai and Ninja Experience"
activities.description: We offer instruction in the traditional Japanese art of sword fighting for beginners and tourists. We also hold trial lessons and shows led by Naniwa Samurai Ambassadors.

activities.name: Mikuni Distillery
activities.description: The only craft gin and whiskey distillery in Osaka City. Located in Tamatsukuri, near Naniwanomiya, Osaka, said to be the first capital of Japan, they produce the floral-flavored "Osaka GIN."

activities.name: Kamigata Onsen Ikkyu
activities.description: Located in the city, close to Universal Studios Japan, this natural hot spring is full of charm, boasting one of the largest open-air baths in the Kansai region and the world's first ultra-fine mist sauna.

activities.name: Nakanoshima LOVE CENTRAL
activities.description: This complex includes an Italian restaurant produced by the popular artist 'DREAMS COME TRUE', a BBQ lounge, a river cruise, and a wedding salon.

activities.name: Kyobashi Coms Garden
activities.description: An underground gourmet mall with an aerial garden that connects to Kyobashi Terminal and Osaka Business Park (OBP). A diverse collection of restaurants, including Japanese and Western, noodle shops, izakayas, and cafes.

activities.name: Sumitomo Life Izumi Hall
activities.description: A shoebox-shaped concert hall with 821 seats, modeled after the home of the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra. It offers an ideal acoustic space for classical music.

activities.name: Creative Japanese confectionery workshop Bashoan Tempozan store
activities.description: Located in Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokocho in Tenpozan, Osaka, this Japanese confectionery shop is popular for its stone mill experience and its signature warabi mochi (bracken starch dumplings).

activities.name: Japanese sword test cutting
activities.description: This dojo allows you to try out cutting with a real Japanese sword. Even beginners can learn authentic swordsmanship and etiquette with peace of mind. Uniforms are available for rent, and there is also a sword shop on-site.

activities.name: Sennichimae Doguyasuji Shopping Street
activities.description: Located in Namba, Osaka, this 150m-long shopping street is lined with specialty shops selling cooking tools and kitchen supplies. In addition to the tools used by professional chefs, you can also enjoy the experience of making food samples.

activities.name: Senbayashi shopping street
activities.description: Located in Asahi Ward, Osaka City, this lively shopping street was once known as "the cheapest in Japan." The approximately 700m arcade is lined with around 200 stores, selling fresh produce, restaurants, household goods and more.

activities.name: Cutely decorated sushi roll experience
activities.description: This is a class where you can easily make sushi rolls in the shape of animals or flowers, just like making crafts.

activities.name: National Bunraku Theatre
activities.description: This theater is where you can watch Bunraku, a traditional Japanese performing art that has been registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

activities.name: Dojima Avanza
activities.description: The office building, with two basement floors and 23 floors above ground, houses a bookstore with one of the largest sales floor areas in the Kansai region, as well as restaurants and general stores. The Dojima Yakushido temple is located in the east plaza.

activities.name: Dojima Crosswalk
activities.description: This commercial complex makes everyday life more convenient and luxurious. It consists of a total of 27 stores, including supermarkets, restaurants, cafes, fitness clubs, and cultural schools.

activities.name: Daimaru Shinsaibashi store
activities.description: This department store, built using the Vories architecture, was renovated in the fall of 2019. It houses over 360 specialty stores, ranging from luxury brands to brands aimed at young people.

activities.name: Daitora Kamaboko Ebisubashisuji Main Branch
activities.description: Established in 1876, we continue to produce delicious kamaboko (fish cakes) and tempura, focusing on fresh conger eel and cherishing refined craftsmanship.

activities.name: Otsuki Noh Theatre
activities.description: Built in 1935, this is one of the few Noh theaters in the Kansai region that survived the war. Guests can enjoy Noh, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, from a seated seat, and a wide range of performances are held, from classics to new works.

activities.name: Popular Theater (Taishu Engeki)
activities.description: You can enjoy popular theater at the prestigious Gofukuza Theater, which has a history of about 100 years, located in Umeda, the center of Osaka. The show consists of two parts: a play themed on Japan's ancient times, and a dance show featuring beautiful costumes and performances.

activities.name: Osaka Wakuwaku Academy
activities.description: This is an experience class in the form of an entertainment show where you can learn about food samples and actually try making them.

activities.name: Osaka City Shinkin Bank Stadium
activities.description: Located within Maishima Sports Island, this is a full-scale baseball stadium where the professional baseball team Orix Buffaloes' Western League official games and amateur baseball tournaments are held.

activities.name: Osaka Station City
activities.description: A huge complex directly connected to JR Osaka Station, it houses commercial facilities such as Lucua and Lucua 1100, a movie theater, and restaurants, allowing you to enjoy shopping and gourmet food all day long.

activities.name: Asue Osaka Pool & Ice Skating Rink
activities.description: This ice skating rink is located in Minato Ward, Osaka City. It is open to the public only during the winter (November to April), and you can experience speedy and beautiful skating.

activities.name: Osaka Helicopter Tour (Ogawa Airlines)
activities.description: This helicopter sightseeing flight service departs from Maishima Heliport and allows you to enjoy the cityscape, bay area, and night view of Osaka from the sky. You can enjoy views of Osaka Castle, the Kita district, Universal Studios Japan, and more from above.

activities.name: Osaka Shiki Theater
activities.description: This is Shiki Theatre Company's first Kansai base theater, which opened in Herbis ENT in Nishi-Umeda, Osaka in November 2004. It has a Western-style theater design that allows for a sense of unity between the approximately 1,200-seat audience and the stage.

activities.name: Osaka International House Center (I-House)
activities.description: This convention facility is equipped with large and small halls, conference rooms, galleries, a hotel, restaurants and other facilities, making it suitable for hosting all kinds of events, from large academic conferences to seminars, concerts and art exhibitions.

activities.name: Osaka Castle Hall
activities.description: Built to commemorate the 400th anniversary of the construction of Osaka Castle, this multi-purpose arena can accommodate up to 16,000 people and is the largest hall in western Japan, hosting concerts, sporting events, exhibitions, and more.

activities.name: Osaka Castle Music Hall
activities.description: Located within the lush greenery of Osaka Castle Park, this outdoor music hall can accommodate approximately 3,000 people. Equipped with sound and lighting equipment, it is widely used for various events such as music concerts and lectures.

activities.name: Osaka City Central Public Hall
activities.description: Located in Nakanoshima, Osaka, this nationally designated Important Cultural Property features a beautiful neo-Renaissance exterior. Since its completion in 1918, it is a historic building that has been involved in the development of culture and art in Osaka.

activities.name: Osaka City Abeno Disaster Prevention Center "Abeno Tascul"
activities.description: This is an experiential disaster prevention learning facility where you can learn disaster prevention knowledge and techniques through hands-on experience in preparation for disasters such as the Nankai Trough megathrust earthquake.

activities.name: Shin Kabukiza
activities.description: The theater is characterized by its immersive seating space, where the performers and audience are close to each other. It is a theater where you can enjoy a wide variety of performances, from troupe performances to musicals and concerts.

activities.name: Kizu Market
activities.description: Osaka's wholesale market boasts a history of over 300 years. It is home to around 150 wholesalers of seafood, fruit and vegetables, and also hosts morning markets and auction experiences for the general public.

activities.name: Osaka Shochikuza
activities.description: This historic theater opened in Dotonbori in 1923 as Japan's first traditional theater. It hosts a wide range of performing arts, including kabuki, contemporary plays, revues, musicals, and concerts.

activities.name: Osaka Water Bus Aqualiner
activities.description: A sightseeing boat lets you view the water city of Osaka from the river. The 40-minute tour takes you around the famous sites and historic sites along the waterfront, including Osaka Castle, Osaka City Central Public Hall, and the retro buildings of Kitahama.

activities.name: Osaka Bay Cruise Santa Maria
activities.description: This sailing ship tours the famous sights of the Osaka Bay area. It is a replica of the Santa Maria, Columbus' flagship that reached the New World, but at approximately twice the size, allowing you to enjoy a relaxing cruise.

activities.name: Osaka Port sailing ship-type sightseeing boat Santa Maria Twilight Cruise
activities.description: Osaka Port is one of the few ports in Japan that faces west, offering beautiful sunsets. Enjoy an elegant 60-minute cruise through the port, illuminated by the setting sun and other sights.

activities.name: Osaka Takashimaya
activities.description: Directly connected to Namba Station on the Nankai Electric Railway and Osaka Metro Midosuji Line, this long-established department store is representative of Osaka's Minami area.

activities.name: Osaka Tsuruhashi Market (near Tsuruhashi Station)
activities.description: This huge market, with around 800 stores, still evokes the retro atmosphere of the time just after the end of the war. It's an international tourist spot with a wide selection of yakiniku, Korean food, fresh fish, clothing, and more.

activities.name: Tenma Tenjin Hanjotei
activities.description: Located on the north side of the Osaka Tenmangu Shrine grounds, this theater specializes in Kamigata Rakugo. It opened in 2006 and holds both daytime and evening performances every day. In addition to Rakugo, it also hosts variety shows such as magic tricks and manzai comedy.

activities.name: Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street
activities.description: Starting from Tenjinbashi and stretching north to Tenjinbashisuji 7-chome, this shopping street is the longest in Japan, with a total length of approximately 2.6 kilometers. It is lined with approximately 800 stores and has a history of thriving as a temple town for Osaka Tenmangu Shrine.

activities.name: Tenjinbashisuji Merchants Association (1-3 Chome)
activities.description: This shopping street, which has developed since the Edo period as a temple town for Osaka Tenmangu Shrine, boasts the longest length in Japan.

activities.name: Oguraya/Ogura Konbu
activities.description: This is Osaka's most traditional kelp shop, with a history spanning over 150 years. They sell products made with carefully selected, top-quality kelp from Hokkaido, as well as award-winning items such as "Sen'o," which showcases the craftsmanship of skilled artisans.

activities.name: Footwear wholesale district
activities.description: Located in the Nipponbashi East district of Naniwa Ward, Osaka City, this historic wholesale district is home to around 100 stores selling sandals, zori, bags, umbrellas and other accessories along its 400m-long street.

activities.name: Yamamoto Noh Theatre (Noh experience)
activities.description: This is the oldest Noh stage in Osaka where you can experience Noh. You can see Noh costumes and masks up close and even take lessons on stage.

activities.name: Shinsaibashi-Suji Shopping Street
activities.description: A typical shopping street in Osaka's Minami area, stretching approximately 580 meters from the south side of Nagahori-dori to Soemoncho-dori, it is lined with approximately 180 clothing stores and restaurants.

activities.name: Ninja House Experience "Ninja Trick House"
activities.description: Located on the 8th floor of the Edion Namba main store, this is an experiential attraction that faithfully recreates a ninja house. In addition to the trick house where you can search for hidden scrolls of secret techniques, you can also enjoy throwing shuriken.

activities.name: Ebisubashisuji shopping street
activities.description: Located in the heart of Minami, Osaka, this shopping street is home to everything from famous, long-established stores that have been in business since the Genroku period to shops at the forefront of cutting-edge fashion.

activities.name: Kenshinkai
activities.description: We convey the ancient traditions of Japan through experiences and demonstrations of traditional martial arts (swordsmanship, jujutsu, ninjutsu, etc.).

activities.name: Former Kuroda Domain Storehouse Nagayamon Gate
activities.description: This is the front gate of the Kuroda clan storehouse from the Edo period, which was located in what is now Nakanoshima, and is a tangible cultural property of Osaka Prefecture. It is one of the few remaining storehouses from the mid-Edo period.

activities.name: Sonezaki Ohatsutenjin Shopping Street
activities.description: Located on the pilgrimage route to Tsuyunoten Shrine, the birthplace of the Sonezaki Shinju story, this friendly shopping street in the Umeda area of northern Osaka is lined with around 100 stores, large and small.

activities.name: Asahi Theater
activities.description: This long-established Shinsekai theater can accommodate 300 people. It's a true "theater" with box seats and a runway. It opened in 1910 and was renovated in 1977 as a theater specializing in popular theater.

activities.name: Panasonic IMP Building
activities.description: A high-rise shopping, amenity, and business complex that represents OBP (Osaka Business Park). It is lined with international fashion stores, general stores, restaurants, and also houses the IMP Hall, which can accommodate approximately 850 people.

activities.name: Matsuyamachi Shopping Street
activities.description: This shopping street in Osaka is lined with over 100 wholesale and specialty stores selling Hina dolls, toys, sweets, and Japanese paper. The selection of products changes with the seasons, including May dolls and fireworks, and is popular with locals and tourists alike.

activities.name: Baisendou/Millwood and Rock Rice
activities.description: This long-established store was founded in the early Edo period and sells Osaka specialties "Awa Okoshi" and "Iwa Okoshi," which are made using traditional methods and have a rich, natural flavor.

activities.name: Umeda Gofukuza Popular Theater
activities.description: One of Japan's leading theaters dedicated to popular theater. Located in a building in Umeda, Osaka, it is an easily accessible location where you can enjoy authentic popular theater. It is fully equipped with stage equipment such as auctions, and foreign staff are always on-site.

activities.name: Umeda Arts Theater Drama City
activities.description: Located a 3-minute walk from the Chayamachi exit of Hankyu Railway's Osaka-Umeda Station, this theater hosts a wide variety of performances, from plays and Takarazuka Revue productions to musicals, classical opera, and ballet.

activities.name: Umeda Arts Theater Main Hall
activities.description: The former Umeda Koma Theater reopened after renovation in 2005. It hosts a wide variety of performances, from musicals to classical opera and ballet. The 1,905-seat stage has the reverberation time and listening level to be ideal for not only plays but also classical music performances.

activities.name: THE DAY BBQ Osaka
activities.description: Located on Maishima, a resort island in the Osaka Bay area, this covered BBQ field has over 500 seats. Enjoy a casual barbecue in the lush natural surroundings without having to bring anything with you.

activities.name: Morinomiya Piloti Hall
activities.description: This multipurpose hall was built using a pilotis system (raised floor) with special beams, which is rare in Japan, in order to preserve the remains and artifacts of the Morinomiya ruins. It is widely used for plays, concerts, dance rehearsals, and more.

activities.name: Morino Sample (Food model making experience)
activities.description: Food samples are an amazing technology that Japan is proud of around the world. On weekends, we hold workshops where you can try your hand at making your own parfait samples.

activities.name: Yodoyabashi Odona
activities.description: Built on the site of the historic Aihi Elementary School, this sophisticated commercial facility supports the lifestyles of working adults.

activities.name: Katayama Photo Studio
activities.description: This historic photo studio, founded in 1923, sells postcards at Osaka Castle Museum. We take commemorative and ID photos in our professional studio.

activities.name: Karahori Shopping Street
activities.description: Stretching east to west for about 800m from Matsuyamachisuji to Tanimachisuji and Kamimachisuji, this shopping street retains a strong pre-war atmosphere. Enjoy strolling through the retro town, lined with cafes and general stores renovated from tenement houses from the early Showa period.

activities.name: Solaniwa Onsen OSAKA BAY TOWER
activities.description: Kansai's largest hot spring theme park is based on the concept of a town from the Azuchi-Momoyama period that has traveled back in time, and combines good old Japanese style with modern Japanese style.

activities.name: Cotton Industry Hall
activities.description: One of Osaka's most retro buildings, it has been designated an Important Cultural Property by the nation. Completed in 1931, it is a masterpiece by architect Setsu Watanabe and is characterized by its luxuriously modern interior.

activities.name: Maikon no Kohara
activities.description: We offer over 200 types of tsukudani, including original tsukudani, such as "Maikon," a fermented kelp made by fermenting and cooking it.Maikon, whose nutritional value is increased by fermentation, can be used as a staple food in the home, or as a gift or souvenir.

activities.name: Maishima Craft Hall
activities.description: A facility that conveys Naniwazu ware, born from the clay on the seabed of Osaka Bay. A diverse pottery workshop that brings together everyone from beginners to professionals.

activities.name: Maishima Sports Island (Maishima Urban Auto Village Barbecue Garden)
activities.description: A vast sports and leisure facility on Maishima, an artificial island in Osaka Bay, where you can enjoy tennis, baseball, car camping, barbecues, etc. It also houses a training ground for a professional soccer team and the Maishima Ceramic Art Museum, where you can try your hand at pottery.

activities.name: Bashodo / Warabimochi (bracken mochi)
activities.description: This long-established store of "warabi mochi" (warabi mochi) has inherited the traditional manufacturing method since it was founded in 1868. You can also experience grinding the finest black beans from Tanba in a stone mill and eating them.

activities.name: Tea Ceremony Experience The Osaka
activities.description: This shop in Dotonbori, Osaka, offers a tea ceremony experience led by an English-speaking tea ceremony instructor. You can learn about the history of the tea ceremony, watch the instructor's tea ceremony, sample the prepared matcha and Japanese sweets, and even try making your own matcha.

activities.name: Traditional Japanese culture experience
activities.description: This dojo is located in Hommachi, Osaka. It offers experiences in traditional Japanese culture, including Iaido (Japanese sword drawing), calligraphy, tea ceremony, and origami. Experienced swordsmen provide instruction, so even beginners can participate with confidence.

activities.name: Kintetsu Art Museum
activities.description: Located on the 8th floor of the Abeno Harukas Kintetsu Main Store Wing Building, this multi-purpose small theater seats up to 322 people and is perfect for stimulating creative direction.

activities.name: KINTETSU department store Abeno Harukas Kintetsu Main Store
activities.description: Located in the 300m high-rise complex "Abeno Harukas," from the second basement floor to the 14th floor, this department store boasts the largest sales floor area in Japan. It offers a wide variety of stores, from world-class brands to one of Japan's largest restaurant areas, with 44 stores.

activities.name: Kintetsu Department Store Hommachi Branch
activities.description: Conveniently located directly connected to Hommachi Station, this compact department store offers a wide selection of food, clothing, large specialty stores, and restaurants.

activities.name: Tsutenkaku Tower Hondori Shopping Street
activities.description: Tsutenkaku Tower is about 200 meters from Ebisucho Station on Osaka Metro Sakaisuji Line. This historic shopping street dates back to the founding of Shinsekai in 1912, and still retains the atmosphere of good old Osaka. It is also a popular photo spot with a direct view of Tsutenkaku Tower.

activities.name: Japan Mint (Factory Tour)
activities.description: This institution manufactures coins, medals, medals of merit, metal crafts, and more. Founded in 1871, it was a pioneer of modern industry. The premises also house the Mint Museum, and the "Cherry Blossom Passage" is held every year in mid-April.

activities.name: Dotonbori Beer Factory
activities.description: The only craft beer factory in Dotonbori, Osaka. Established in 1996, the brand "Dotonbori Beer" is served fresh at the attached Japanese beer restaurant.

activities.name: Hankai Electric Tramway
activities.description: This is the only remaining streetcar in Osaka Prefecture. It connects Tsutenkaku Tower area to Sakai, and is dotted with tourist attractions such as Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine.

activities.name: Hankyu Umeda Main Store
activities.description: One of Japan's largest department stores, it opened in 1929 as the world's first terminal department store. It is a "theater-style department store" that stocks the latest fashion and lifestyle items, and hosts a variety of events in its open-air festival plaza.

activities.name: Hankyu Men's Osaka (HEP Navio)
activities.description: A specialty store featuring cutting-edge luxury and fashion brands exclusively for men.

activities.name: Hankyu Sanban-gai
activities.description: Directly connected to Hankyu Osaka Umeda Station and adjacent to the Hankyu Expressway Bus Terminal, this shopping center has approximately 250 stores.

activities.name: Hankyu Higashidori Shopping Street
activities.description: Osaka Kita's largest entertainment district. Stretching east from Umeda on the Hankyu Railway side, this shopping street is lined with restaurants, bars, snack bars, karaoke, game centers, and other nightlife spots.

activities.name: Hanshin Umeda Main Store
activities.description: This department store in Umeda, Osaka, is affectionately known as "Hanshin of Food." It is popular for its food floor, which has its famous grilled squid, and its Hanshin Tigers shop.

activities.name: Making food samples
activities.description: In Namba Sennichimae, central Osaka, you can experience making traditional wax food samples. You can take them home on the day, making this a popular pop culture experience for tourists.

activities.name: Design Pocket Main Store, a specialty food replica store
activities.description: Located in Namba, Osaka, this specialty shop sells food sample trinkets and offers hands-on food sample making experiences. You can enjoy creating realistic-looking food samples.

activities.name: Tsurumi Ryokuchi Pool
activities.description: This indoor heated pool is open all year round and is located on the site of the 1990 International Garden and Greenery Exposition. This dome-shaped facility has a tropical atmosphere and offers water slides, a lazy river, and a summer-only outdoor pool.

activities.name: SPACE9
activities.description: This multipurpose event space is located on the 9th floor of the Abeno Harukas Kintetsu Main Store Wing Building. It can be used for a variety of purposes, including dance lessons, meetings, and small experimental events.

activities.name: TAIKO-LAB Umekita
activities.description: The largest Taiko drumming studio in the Kansai region, with a wide range of attendees from beginners to experienced drummers! People of all ages, from 3 to 90 years old, can enjoy Taiko drumming.

activities.name: TOHO CINEMAS Namba
activities.description: For those who want a high-quality movie experience, this theater offers a comfortable space for a wide range of people, from couples to families, as well as immersive images and sound.

activities.name: bern
activities.description: A hair salon in the Umeda, Nakatsu, and Fukushima area specializing in hair quality improvement and hair straightening. We offer a private space with semi-private booths for all seats, and also provide hair growth treatments using human stem cell culture fluid.

food.description: Recommended for those who want to experience Japanese KAWAII culture for themselves. The space is perfect for social media, decorated with illustrations by popular illustrator Project C.K. It is completely non-smoking and alcohol-free, so even children can enjoy themselves with peace of mind.

food.name_ja: 北浜レトロビルヂング
food.description: This cafe has an antique British atmosphere and is located in a building that was completed in 1912 and is a registered tangible cultural property of Japan. Its afternoon tea sets and homemade cakes are popular.

food.name_ja: 幸せのフクロウカフェchouette
food.description: Located in Shinsaibashi, Osaka, this is one of Japan's largest owl cafes, offering a relaxing experience where you can interact with 22 owls representing 17 different species.
