sights.name: Osaka Castle Main Keep (Osaka Castle Museum)
sights.description: A symbol of Osaka. 55 meters above ground, with 5 floors and 8 stories, this historic castle was started by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The current building was rebuilt in 1931 and is a registered tangible cultural property of Japan.

sights.name: Dotonbori
sights.description: Dotonbori, lined with giant three-dimensional billboards such as Shochikuza, Kani Doraku, and the Glico sign, is a representative entertainment district in Osaka's Minami area. You can enjoy food and live entertainment.

sights.name: Tsutenkaku Tower
sights.description: Osaka's landmark tower is registered as a national tangible cultural property. Popular attractions include the golden observation deck, the Billiken statue, and the tower slider.

sights.name: KAIYUKAN
sights.description: This is one of the world's largest aquariums, representing Osaka, and faithfully recreates the natural environment of the Pacific Ocean, the world's largest ocean, and its surrounding waters.

sights.name: Shitennoji Temple
sights.description: Founded by Prince Shotoku in 593, it was the first official temple of Buddhism in Japan. The temple has survived numerous war disasters and retains the Shitennoji style of temple layout, which conveys the oldest style in Japan.

sights.name: Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine
sights.description: It is the head shrine of the approximately 2,300 Sumiyoshi shrines across the country and is the Ichinomiya of Settsu Province.

sights.name: Umeda Sky Building KUCHU-TEIEN OBSERVATORY
sights.description: One of the landmarks of Umeda, Osaka, the open-air rooftop observation deck is popular, offering a 360-degree view of Osaka's cityscape from a height of 173 meters above ground.

sights.name: Shinsekai
sights.description: This downtown area in the southern part of Osaka City is famous for Tsutenkaku Tower Janjan Yokocho, and a large puffer fish lantern sign. You can enjoy gourmet food such as kushikatsu and doteyaki, as well as a retro atmosphere.

sights.name: Nakanoshima Park
sights.description: This waterside park is sandwiched between the Dojima River and the Tosabori River. It has a rose garden with 3,700 roses of 310 different varieties, and its harmonious scenery with the surrounding retro buildings has earned it the title of one of Osaka's 100 best green spaces.

sights.name: Osaka Castle Park
sights.description: Located in the center of Osaka, this vast park covers a total area of 105.6 hectares. In addition to historical buildings such as Osaka Castle Museum, it is also home to numerous spots where you can enjoy seasonal flowers such as cherry blossoms and plum blossoms.

sights.name: Osaka Tennoji Zoo
sights.description: This zoo has a history of over 100 years. Its popular "ecological exhibits" recreate the landscapes of animal habitats, such as the African Savannah Zone.

sights.name: Osaka Museum of History
sights.description: This museum studies and introduces the history and culture of Osaka spanning nearly 1,400 years. It displays the history from ancient times to the present day through full-scale reconstructions and models.

sights.name: Hozenji Yokocho Alley
sights.description: Located in the bustling Minami area of Osaka, this charming stone-paved alley is lined with renowned restaurants and eateries, centered around Mizukake Fudoson.

sights.name: GLION MUSEUM
sights.description: This museum, housed in a renovated red brick warehouse built in 1923, displays approximately 80 precious classic cars from Japan and abroad.

sights.name: OBP (Osaka Business Park)
sights.description: Osaka's new city center boasts a site of 26 hectares. In addition to corporate offices, the complex is home to Osaka Castle Hall, shopping facilities, hotels, and more.

sights.name: OCAT (Osaka City Air Terminal)
sights.description: Directly connected to JR Namba Station, this is the largest bus terminal in western Japan. In addition to being the departure and arrival point for airport limousine buses and express buses, this complex also features shopping, restaurants, and a rooftop garden.

sights.name: hu+gMUSEUM
sights.description: Located in the birthplace of Osaka Gas, this is an information hub for food and housing. It is a showroom where you can see, touch, taste, and experience the rich lifestyles that gas can make possible.

sights.name: Gamoyon neighborhood (Gamo 4-chome)
sights.description: This area is attracting attention for the "Gamoyon Nigiwai Project," a town development project that renovated old houses while preserving the atmosphere of a downtown area. It is popular as a food town lined with retro and modern restaurants.

sights.name: Museum of Living (Ganko Hiranogo House)
sights.description: This museum is located on the grounds of the Japanese restaurant "Ganko Hiranogoyashiki" in Hirano Ward, Osaka City. Housed in a renovated Edo period village headman's residence, it displays kimonos, pottery, hanging scrolls and other everyday items that evoke Kawachi culture.

sights.name: Sakishima CosmoTower Observatory
sights.description: 252 meters above ground, this magnificent, 360-degree panoramic observation space offers unobstructed views of the Osaka Bay area, Awaji Island, the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge, Kansai International Airport, and more.

sights.name: Tonbori River Walk
sights.description: The Dotonbori waterfront promenade is impressive with its beautiful neon lights reflected on the water's surface. It's also a spot where the Tenjin Festival and Kabuki boat processions take place.

sights.name: MIRACLE WORLD
sights.description: A 20-minute mini cruise of Dotonbori. Guided by an Osaka guide crew, you'll enjoy learning about the inside stories of famous spots and hidden highlights.

sights.name: Namba Grand Kagetsu
sights.description: The Hall of Comedy is a place where the best comedians in Japan gather. From veteran comedians who are the hall's flagship performers to popular young comedians, you can enjoy Yoshimoto Shinkigeki, manzai, and rakugo from morning to night, 365 days a year.

sights.name: Thermos Memorial Museum
sights.description: This museum showcases the 90-year history of Zojirushi Thermos' manufacturing and technological evolution. You can experience and learn about the evolution of the thermos and the wonders of vacuum.

sights.name: Americamura
sights.description: Osaka Minami is a unique town that is the most vibrant and dynamic part of the Kansai region, and a leader in youth culture.

sights.name: Kids Plaza Osaka
sights.description: This is Japan's first full-scale children's museum. It is filled with exhibits and workshops where children can learn while having fun, discovering the wonders of science, encountering world cultures and play.

sights.name: Cosmo Square
sights.description: This district in the Osaka Bay Area is home to a concentration of cutting-edge technology development companies, convention facilities such as Intex Osaka, WTC, and ATC, as well as cultural and amenity facilities, and is well-equipped with a variety of business support functions.

sights.name: Knowledge Capital
sights.description: Experience cutting-edge technology, products under development, and new ideas as you play with the "future." A large intellectual entertainment space that can be enjoyed by adults and children alike.

sights.name: Peace Osaka (Osaka International Peace Center)
sights.description: This peace museum, which tells the story of the Osaka air raids, opened in a corner of Osaka Castle Park in 1991. It was renovated in 2015 and now commemorates the victims of the Osaka air raids and exhibits materials praying for peace.

sights.name: Mizuno Sportology Gallery
sights.description: This gallery displays the history of Mizuno, known for its motto of "Let's make something great," as well as the history of sports and the latest technology. You can enjoy the exhibits of valuable baseball equipment and uniforms for free.

sights.name: Miraiza Osaka Castle
sights.description: This facility is located in a prime location right in front of the castle tower, allowing you to enjoy a leisurely meal and shopping. This historic building, originally built in 1931 as the headquarters of the 4th Army Division, has been renovated and reborn as a shop, restaurant, and museum.

sights.name: LEGOLAND® Discovery Center Osaka
sights.description: This indoor family-friendly experience facility in Tempozan, Osaka, is home to millions of LEGO® blocks. There are plenty of attractions where you can experience the world of LEGO, including a 4D cinema and Miniland, which recreates the streets of Osaka.

sights.name: Bandaiike Park
sights.description: Bandai Pond, named after the legend of Prince Shotoku's defeat of a demon, is a peaceful park where migratory birds and humans can relax. The pond, which is about 700 meters in circumference, attracts cherry blossom viewers during the cherry blossom season and migratory birds in the winter.

sights.name: Sanko Shrine
sights.description: Sanko Shrine in Tennoji Ward, Osaka City, is known as the shrine for protecting against paralysis, and is a historic shrine where the "Sanada Loophole" remains as part of "Sanadamaru," a place associated with Sanada Yukimura.

sights.name: Mitsudera Temple (Daifuku-in)
sights.description: This esoteric Buddhist temple was founded by Gyoki Bodhisattva in 744. Located along Midosuji in Shinsaibashi, Osaka, the main hall, rebuilt in 1808, is a valuable relic that escaped war damage.

sights.name: Kamigata Ukiyo-e Museum
sights.description: The world's only permanent ukiyo-e museum, which mainly houses and exhibits paintings of popular actors from the Bunka and Bunsei periods of the late Edo period, offers visitors the opportunity to enjoy Kamigata ukiyo-e, which are characterized by their realistic depictions.

sights.name: Nakanoshima
sights.description: The Nakasu area, surrounded by water and greenery between the Dojima River and Tosabori River, which flow through the center of Osaka, is home to a concentration of administrative, economic, and cultural facilities.

sights.name: Nakanoshima Festival Tower/Nakanoshima Festival Tower West
sights.description: A landmark of Nakanoshima. A complex containing offices, restaurants, shops, the Festival Hall, a hotel, and an art museum within its 200m-tall twin towers.

sights.name: Nakaza Kuidaore Building
sights.description: A gourmet and entertainment complex where you will be greeted by Kuidaore Taro, the symbol of Dotonbori, Osaka. It is scheduled to reopen in the spring of 2025.

sights.name: Kyuhoji Bridge
sights.description: This is one of the oldest bridges in Osaka, spanning the Higashi-Yokobori River, dating back to the time of Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Currently, it is a Gerber-type reinforced concrete bridge characterized by its dark green railings and cleanly designed streetlights.

sights.name: Imamiya Ebisu Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is worshipped as the Osaka god of business, Ebessan. Every January, over one million people visit the shrine during the Toka Ebisu festival, and the place is bustling with activity.

sights.name: Imahashi
sights.description: This historic bridge spans the Higashi-Yokobori River and even appears in the "Osaka Campaign Map." During the Edo period, the surrounding area was lined with money changers and flourished as a financial center.

sights.name: Denpozan Saienji Temple
sights.description: Founded by the hermit Hodo in the first year of the Taika era (645), this temple is said to be the oldest place in Japan where Buddhism was introduced.

sights.name: Sumiyoshi Park
sights.description: Osaka's oldest park, opened in 1873. Adjacent to Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine, it is home to the historic "Takatoro" lantern and a stone monument bearing a haiku poem by Matsuo Basho, and is a popular cherry blossom viewing spot in the spring, attracting many visitors.

sights.name: Shinano Bridge
sights.description: This bridge once spanned the Nishiyokobori River, and is now a historical spot where a stone monument remains. There are records dating back to the Genroku period (1688-1704), and the surrounding area was once lined with lumber merchants and china merchants.

sights.name: Senkoji Temple
sights.description: Located in Hirano Ward, Osaka City, this temple is famous for allowing visitors to experience hell and paradise. Popular experiences include being judged by King Enma in the Jigoku-do Hall and meditating surrounded by mandalas in the Land of Buddha experience.

sights.name: Hachikenyahama Pier
sights.description: During the Edo period, this wharf flourished as a departure point for the 30-koku boats connecting Kyoto and Osaka. Today, it has been revived as a port where you can enjoy cruising and is a symbol of the water city of Osaka, serving as a place of relaxation for people.

sights.name: Enjuan (Kama Hachiman)
sights.description: This temple is famous for praying for victory, and it is said that during the Winter Siege of Osaka, Sanada Yukimura prayed for victory by driving a sickle into a sacred tree, achieving a great victory.

sights.name: Kitamido (Tsumura Betsuin)
sights.description: This Jodo Shinshu Honganji temple is the origin of the name of Midosuji, a street that runs north and south through Osaka City. It was moved to its current location in 1597 and has now been rebuilt as a modern main hall.

sights.name: Minamihorie and Kitahorie areas
sights.description: The Horie area is gaining attention as a fashionable part of Osaka. Centered around Tachibana Street, once known as a town of furniture, it is now a trendsetting area with cafes, general stores, and apparel shops.

sights.name: Minamisemba
sights.description: This trendsetting area in Osaka's Minami district is home to a unique lineup of shops, including stylish open-terrace cafes, designer shops, and hair salons that offer unique styles.

sights.name: Kuchinawazaka
sights.description: Located in Tennoji Ward, Osaka City, this is one of the "Seven Hills of Tennoji." The name comes from the fact that the undulating road resembles a snake (kuchinawa) when viewed from the bottom. This quiet, stone-paved slope is also known for its monument to the author, Sakunosuke Oda.

sights.name: Manshozan Kichijoji (Temple of the Loyal Samurai)
sights.description: This is the family temple of the Osaka Asano clan, and it is home to the graves of Asano Takumi-no-kami and the 47 loyal retainers, famous from the Chushingura story. The Osaka Gishi Festival is held here every year on the second Sunday of December.

sights.name: Abiko-san Daisho Kannon-ji Temple (Abiko Kannon)
sights.description: Japan's oldest temple of Kannon Bodhisattva. Founded in the 7th year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (546), it enshrines a statue of Kannon given as a gift by King Seong of Baekje.

sights.name: Suomachi Street (Europe Street)
sights.description: The streets of Shinsaibashi in Osaka, lined with cobblestones and streetlights, exude an elegant atmosphere. Lined with stylish boutiques, restaurants, and galleries, it is a popular area for adults.

sights.name: Sakuyakonohanakan
sights.description: One of Japan's leading comprehensive botanical museums, it displays approximately 15,000 plants of 5,500 species that grow in various climates around the world, including rare flowers such as the Himalayan blue poppy.

sights.name: Shitennoji Koshindo
sights.description: This is the place where the first Koshin statue in Japan appeared, and the principal image is Shomen Kongo Doji (a secret Buddha). It has a history of 1,300 years, and it is revered as a place where if you visit on Koshin day or the day before, your wish will come true.

sights.name: Kokubunji Temple, Settsu Province (Head temple of the Kokubunji branch of the Shingon sect)
sights.description: Located in Kita-ku, Osaka City, this temple is the head temple of the Shingon sect of Buddhism's Kokubunji school. Founded 1,350 years ago, it became a Kokubunji temple during the reign of Emperor Shomu.

sights.name: The National Museum of Art, Osaka
sights.description: Located in Nakanoshima, Osaka, this completely underground art museum is a globally rare sight. It houses approximately 8,200 pieces of artwork, mainly contemporary art, and is characterized by its exterior design that evokes the vitality of bamboo.

sights.name: Zama Shrine
sights.description: The local deity of Senba, Osaka. Worshipped as the god of protection for homes, safe travels, and safe childbirth, the shrine is also known as the birthplace of the Watanabe family name.

sights.name: Shirokita Park
sights.description: This historic park in Osaka's Asahi Ward opened in 1934 on the banks of the Yodo River.

sights.name: Johoku Iris Garden
sights.description: This strolling iris garden, covering an area of approximately 1.3 hectares, has been selected as one of the "100 Best Green Areas in Osaka." It cultivates approximately 13,000 irises of 250 varieties, including Edo, Ise, and Higo varieties.

sights.name: Horikawa Ebisu Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is located in Kita-ku, Osaka City. It enshrines Hiruko-no-Okami, who is beloved as the god of prosperity in business. It is crowded with many worshippers during the Toka Ebisu festival.

sights.name: Horikoshi Shrine
sights.description: One of the seven shrines of Shitennoji Temple, built by Prince Shotoku in memory of his uncle, Emperor Sushun, the 32nd emperor. A power spot in Tennoji, Osaka, known for its deity who grants one wish in a lifetime.

sights.name: Zofukuji Temple
sights.description: This temple is associated with Usuda Hayato (Iwami Jutaro), a Toyotomi military commander who played an active role in the Battle of Osaka.

sights.name: Dainenbutsuji Temple
sights.description: It is the head temple of the Yuzunenbutsu sect, and its main hall is the largest wooden building in Osaka Prefecture. It is known for events such as the "Manbe Oneri," which has been designated an intangible folk cultural property of Osaka City.

sights.name: Oebashi
sights.description: One of the five bridges built over the Dojima River during the Genroku period, the current bridge was designed and completed in the early Showa period through a design competition, and is a beautiful arch bridge that represents modern Osaka architecture.

sights.name: The Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
sights.description: Japan's first housing museum, where you can see a life-size reproduction of Osaka's townscape from the late Edo period, and experience Osaka homes from the Meiji, Taisho, and Showa periods.

sights.name: Osaka Cathedral (St. Mary's Cathedral)
sights.description: Built on the site of the Hosokawa family estate, this Catholic cathedral features stone statues of Hosokawa Gracia and Takayama Ukon. Its highlights include 100 stained glass windows, murals by Domoto Insho, and a 2,400-pipe organ.

sights.name: Nakanoshima Museum of Art, Osaka
sights.description: The museum aims to be a platform with communication and creativity, centered around a collection of modern and contemporary art and design from Osaka and around the world.

sights.name: Osaka Entrepreneurs' Museum
sights.description: This museum displays and introduces the achievements of 108 entrepreneurs who were active in Osaka, along with related items. Operated by the Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, it aims to promote entrepreneurial spirit and develop the next generation of people.

sights.name: Osaka Club
sights.description: This building is one of Osaka's three most famous buildings and has been used as a club for Osaka's business leaders for over 100 years. It was designed in Southern European style by Yasui Takeo in 1924 and is a registered tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Osaka Exchange
sights.description: This retro building features a magnificent cylindrical white exterior and a beautiful entrance lobby with stained glass. It carries on the history of the Yodoya Rice Market of the Edo period and the Dojima Rice Exchange, the world's first futures exchange.

sights.name: Osaka Castle Gozabune (Golden Ship)
sights.description: Take a 20-minute cruise around the inner moat of Osaka Castle on a golden Japanese boat, modeled after Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Houou Maru. You'll get a close-up look at Japan's tallest stone walls and castle tower.

sights.name: Nishinomaru Garden of Osaka Castle
sights.description: Located within Osaka Castle Park, which spreads out around Osaka Castle Museum, this approximately 6.5 hectare lawn garden is said to have been the residence of Toyotomi Hideyoshi's wife, Kita no Mandokoro.

sights.name: Osaka Tenmangu Shrine
sights.description: Located in the Tenma area near Osaka Station, this shrine is affectionately known as "Tenma no Tenjin-san." It enshrines Sugawara no Michizane, the god of learning and performing arts, and every July it hosts the Tenjin Festival, one of Japan's three major festivals.

sights.name: Osaka City Sewerage Science Museum
sights.description: This new Sewerage Science Museum will turn all your questions about sewers into questions! Everyone from children to adults can have fun learning about sewers, a lifeline we all rely on.

sights.name: Osaka Science Museum
sights.description: The theme of the museum is "Space and Energy," and there are about 200 interactive exhibits, as well as science shows and a planetarium that can be enjoyed by people of all ages.

sights.name: Osaka Municipal Museum of Fine Arts
sights.description: This long-established art museum in Tennoji Park has a history of over 85 years and a collection of over 8,500 pieces, including paintings, sculptures, and crafts from Japan and China.

sights.name: Osaka Museum of Natural History
sights.description: This museum allows you to learn about Osaka's nature, the evolution of living things, and the history of life on Earth. It features impressive exhibits such as a life-size replica of a Naumann's elephant, whale skeletons, and dinosaur skeletons.

sights.name: Osaka Municipal Nagai Botanical Garden
sights.description: Nagai Botanical Garden is one of Japan's leading botanical gardens, beloved as an "urban oasis" brimming with nature and greenery.

sights.name: Osaka Regional Environmental Facilities Association Maishima Factory
sights.description: This innovative and colorful waste disposal plant was designed by the Viennese artist Friedensreich Hundertwasser. It is a facility themed around environmental protection and coexistence with nature, and is open to the public for free.

sights.name: Osaka Prefectural Kamigata Performing Arts Museum Wahha Kamigata
sights.description: The only museum in the country with a laughter-themed theme where you can experience the charm of Kamigata performing arts such as manzai and rakugo.

sights.name: Osaka Prefectural Nakanoshima Library
sights.description: This stately building features three stone stories and a towering copper-roofed dome. It has been designated an Important Cultural Property of Japan and houses documents related to Osaka, classics, and books related to business.

sights.name: Osaka Cultural Center, Tempozan
sights.description: In 2013, the former Suntory Museum was renamed "Osaka Culturarium Tempozan." The gallery is a facility that hosts a variety of exhibitions, including fascinating and topical special exhibitions, as well as natural history and art exhibitions.

sights.name: Osaka Science and Technology Museum
sights.description: This free science museum is run by Japan's leading cutting-edge companies and research institutes, who use hands-on exhibits and games to introduce the latest science and technology in everyday life in an easy-to-understand manner.

sights.name: Tempozan Harbor Village
sights.description: This comprehensive bay area leisure spot is centered around the world's largest aquarium, Kaiyukan. It also houses a marketplace where you can enjoy gourmet food, shopping, and entertainment, as well as the Santa Maria sightseeing boat.

sights.name: Tempozan Park
sights.description: This park is home to Mount Tempo, famous for being the lowest mountain in Japan (4.5m above sea level). The beautifully maintained cherry blossoms and pine trees have made it a hidden cherry blossom viewing spot.

sights.name: Tennoji Seven Hills
sights.description: This is the collective name for the seven slopes in Tennoji Ward, Osaka City: Shingonzaka, Genshojizaka, Kuchinawazaka, Aizenzaka, Kiyomizuzaka, Tenjinzaka, and Osaka.

sights.name: TEN-SHIBA(Tennoji Park Entrance Area )
sights.description: In addition to the open lawn space (Ten-Shiba) and tenants (restaurants, soccer court, etc.), the park plaza is located near the Osaka Tennoji Zoo, Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts, Japanese garden (Keitakuen), etc.

sights.name: Tenjinzaka
sights.description: One of the Seven Hills of Tennoji, this historic slope leads to Yasui Shrine, which enshrines Sugawara no Michizane, and has long been known as a place with excellent water.

sights.name: Tenjinbashi
sights.description: This bridge crosses over Nakanoshima's "Sword Stakes" and spans the Okawa River (formerly the Yodo River). Along with Tenmabashi and Naniwabashi, it is known as one of the "Three Great Bridges of Naniwa," and is a historic structure said to have been built around 1594.

sights.name: Taiheiji Temple (Temple of the Thirteen Pilgrimages)
sights.description: This temple in Tennoji, Osaka, is known for the tradition of "Jusan Mairi," where people receive wisdom and good fortune from Kokuzo Bosatsu at the age of thirteen (according to the Japanese age reckoning system).

sights.name: Tairyuji Temple
sights.description: This ancient temple in Umeda, Osaka was founded by Kobo Daishi, also known as Kukai. The principal image is a Thousand-Armed Kannon statue, and the temple grounds also contain the grave of Yodo-dono. It is also known as a place associated with the Freedom and People's Rights Movement.

sights.name: Abe no Seimei Shrine
sights.description: This is the legendary birthplace of Abe no Seimei, a popular onmyoji (exorcist) who has been gaining popularity in recent years.

sights.name: Yasui Shrine
sights.description: This ancient shrine enshrines Sukunahikona-no-kami and Sugawara no Michizane. It is known as the place where Sanada Yukimura died in battle during the Summer Siege of Osaka, and a monument to Yukimura has been erected within the grounds.

sights.name: Soemoncho
sights.description: Located in Osaka's Minami district, this historic entertainment district has flourished since ancient times. It is a popular tourist spot with a wide range of establishments, from high-end clubs and famous restaurants to more affordable eateries, and its beautiful neon lights at night.

sights.name: Hoju-in Temple
sights.description: This Shingon Buddhist temple was founded by Kukai in 825. The principal image of worship is Dainichi Nyorai. It has a history linked to Sugawara no Michizane, and also houses a statue of Maitreya Bodhisattva from the Kamakura period.

sights.name: Jakkoji Temple (Kimido Hall at Eguchi)
sights.description: This temple was founded by Koso Bikuni, the daughter of Taira no Sukemori. It is widely known for the legend that the monk Saigyo and Lady Eguchi exchanged poems here.

sights.name: Teranishi family Abeno tenement house
sights.description: This historic building is the first row house in Japan to be registered as a national tangible cultural property. It is a two-story wooden row house with four houses built in 1932 and is currently used as a restaurant.

sights.name: Sukunahikona Shrine
sights.description: Located among the buildings of Doshomachi, Osaka's "medicine town," this shrine is known as the god of health and medicine. It enshrines Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto, the ancestor of Japanese medicine, and Shennong Yantei, the ancestor of Chinese medicine.

sights.name: Kawaguchi Christian Church
sights.description: This chapel was built in the foreign settlement established in the Kawaguchi area following the opening of Osaka Port in 1868. Completed in 1920, it is a Gothic-style brick building and is designated as a national tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Kawasaki Bridge
sights.description: This cable-stayed bridge for bicycles and pedestrians crosses the Okawa River, connecting Tenma in Kita-ku and Amijima-cho in Miyakojima-ku, Osaka.

sights.name: Kawabata Yasunari Literary Monument
sights.description: This monument is inscribed with a passage from "Soribashi" (Soribashi Bridge), written by Osaka-born Nobel Prize-winning author Yasunari Kawabata. Located within the grounds of Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine, it is a popular spot for literature fans.

sights.name: Toyasu Bridge
sights.description: This bridge was built over the Tosabori River by Yodoya Tsuneyasu, a lumber merchant in the Edo period. It connects Kita-ku and Nishi-ku in Osaka City, and conveys the history of Yodoya, who was instrumental in the development of Nakanoshima.

sights.name: Yae Shrine
sights.description: Yaei Shrine is a shrine in Ikuno Ward, Osaka City, that was founded during the Bunroku era by transferring a branch of the spirit from Kumano Shrine, a former national shrine in Shimane Prefecture.

sights.name: Midosuji Sculpture Street
sights.description: Along Osaka's main street, Midosuji, 29 sculptures by famous artists from Japan and abroad, including Rodin, Henry Moore, and Takamura Kotaro, are on display. Stretching approximately 4km from Umeda to Namba, this is a spot where you can casually stroll around and enjoy art appreciation.

sights.name: Miyuki Street (Korea Town)
sights.description: Japan's largest Koreatown is lined with approximately 150 Korean grocery stores, restaurants, and traditional clothing stores. You can enjoy local delicacies such as kimchi and chijimi, as well as hands-on Korean culture classes.

sights.name: Mitsu Park (Triangle Park)
sights.description: This is a landmark and meeting spot in America-mura, a town that nurtured Kansai youth culture. It is a popular place of relaxation, with people enjoying street performances by young comedians and the surrounding takoyaki shops.

sights.name: Mitsumiya (Mitsu Hachiman Shrine)
sights.description: Located in the busy Minami district of Osaka, this shrine has a history of over 1,000 years and is known as the guardian deity of the Shinsaibashi and Americamura areas.

sights.name: Goryo Shrine
sights.description: This shrine was revered as the tutelary deity of the former Tsumura district in Settsu Province, encompassing areas such as Senba, Nakanoshima, Kyomachibori, and Utsubo. It is also known as the birthplace of Bunraku puppetry.

sights.name: Shinganji Temple
sights.description: This temple stands on the site believed to be the location of "Sanada Maru," a fortress built by Sanada Yukimura during the Winter Siege of Osaka. It was rebuilt to commemorate Sanada Yukimura and his son, Daisuke.

sights.name: Shikinagayoshi Shrine
sights.description: It is a shrine listed in the Engishiki (an ancient Japanese legal code), and it is said to have been established around the early Heian period (794 AD), about 1200 years ago. The enshrined deities are Nagae no Sotsuhiko no Mikoto and Kotoshironushi no Mikoto.

sights.name: Aizen-do Shoman-in Temple (Aizen-san)
sights.description: Built by Prince Shotoku, this temple is dedicated to Aizen Myoo, a deity famous for bringing good luck in marriage and marital harmony. It is known for the Aizen Festival, one of Osaka's three major summer festivals, and the Tahoto Pagoda, an important cultural property.

sights.name: Keitakuen Garden
sights.description: Located within Tennoji Park is a purely Japanese-style strolling garden with a forest and spring.

sights.name: Oden-in Temple
sights.description: As an open temple, people gather here for various cultural activities. The main hall is a hall called "Theatrical Oden-in," which is used by many artists as a gallery and performance stage.

sights.name: Ogimachi Park
sights.description: Conveniently located within walking distance of Umeda, this oasis in the city is always filled with cheers and cheers, with large playground equipment, a grassy area, and a pool.

sights.name: Hiyoshi Shrine
sights.description: Located in Asahi Ward, Osaka City, this historic shrine dates back to the Muromachi period. The summer festival in July features processions, lion dances, and kagura dances.

sights.name: United Church of Christ in Japan Naniwa Church
sights.description: Completed in 1930, this retro building features an exterior decorated with Gothic-style spire windows and yellow and green tinted glass, and a chapel with a clean and beautiful space. It was constructed under the design guidance of William Merrell Vories.

sights.name: Japan Crafts Museum
sights.description: This museum exhibits and preserves folk crafts (folk art), from ceramics from various regions such as Old Tamba and Old Seto to contemporary works. It is currently closed for reconstruction.

sights.name: Nipponbashi
sights.description: This bridge was built during the Edo period. Over the years, the area has transformed and developed into a post town, a used bookstore district, and an electronics district. Today, it is also known as the base of Den-Den Town, Osaka's leading electronics district.

sights.name: Nipponbashi Denden Town
sights.description: The largest electric town and otaku district in western Japan, this shopping district has over 150 stores selling highly specialized items such as anime, games, figurines, electronic parts, and audio equipment.

sights.name: Bank of Japan Osaka Branch Old Building
sights.description: Built in 1903 (Meiji 36), this authentic Western-style two-story stone building with a beautiful patina-colored cupola was modeled after the National Bank of Belgium and other buildings. It was designed by Tatsuno Kingo and others.

sights.name: Former Konishi Family Residence Museum
sights.description: This is the former office building of Konishi Co., Ltd., which manufactures and sells the synthetic adhesive "Bond." The building, completed in 1903 with a front-facing design, is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan as a culmination of modern Osaka townhouse architecture.

sights.name: Meijiya Building
sights.description: Located in Sakaisuji Hommachi, this neo-renaissance style retro Taisho era building was completed in 1924 and was known as a source of sophisticated Western food culture at the time.

sights.name: Meiji Bridge
sights.description: This is the site of a bridge that was built over the former Tatsumichi Horikawa River in 1876. A monument now stands here, conveying the history of Osaka.

sights.name: Hommachi Bridge
sights.description: This bridge is said to have been built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi when he constructed Osaka Castle, as part of the excavation of the Higashi-Yokobori River. It is the oldest bridge still in use in Osaka City.

sights.name: Kumata Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 862 during the early Heian period, this shrine is the guardian deity of Hirano Ward, Osaka City, and was established by Sakanoue no Tamuramaro's grandson, Todo. The three shrine buildings are designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan.

sights.name: Sendannoki Bridge (Sandalwood Bridge)
sights.description: Located in the heart of Nakanoshima, Osaka, this viewpoint offers panoramic views of historical buildings such as the Osaka City Central Public Hall and the Osaka Prefectural Nakanoshima Library.

sights.name: Umeda BIGMAN
sights.description: A popular meeting spot in Osaka's Kita area. Powerful images and sounds are projected onto a large 200-inch screen.

sights.name: Shorenji Temple
sights.description: Shorenji Temple, located in Konohana Ward, Osaka City, is a Nichiren Buddhist temple known for its "Kawa Segaki," one of Japan's three major Segaki ceremonies. The ceremony, held annually on August 26th, is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Osaka City.

sights.name: Kema Sakuranomiya Park
sights.description: A riverside park of water, greenery, and cherry blossoms that runs along the riverbed from Kemaaraizeki Weir to Tenmabashi Bridge.

sights.name: Kema Lock
sights.description: This sluice gate connects the Yodo River and Okawa River, which have different water levels, allowing passage. The former No. 1 Lock Gate and the former Wash Weir, completed in 1907, are valuable brick structures and have been designated as Important Cultural Properties of Japan.

sights.name: Suisho Bridge
sights.description: This historic pedestrian bridge was originally built as a movable weir over the Dojima River. Its beautiful arch structure and nighttime illuminations make it a popular spot for strolling around the modern architecture of Nakanoshima, Osaka.

sights.name: Esaki Memorial Hall
sights.description: The Ezaki Glico Museum was built in 1972 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the founding of Glico. It displays past product packaging, advertisements, Glico toys, and items related to the company's founder, Riichi Ezaki.

sights.name: Senpukan
sights.description: Built in 1871 (Meiji 4) as a reception room for the Mint, this all-brick building is a masterpiece of veranda colonial style architecture. It was designated an Important Cultural Property by the Emperor Meiji.

sights.name: Hoanji Temple
sights.description: This historic temple is said to have been built by Prince Shotoku about 1,400 years ago. It enshrines Benzaiten, one of the Seven Lucky Gods of Osaka, and houses a standing statue of Shokannon, a nationally designated important cultural property.

sights.name: Horakuji Temple
sights.description: This temple was founded in 1178 by Taira no Shigemori, the eldest son of Taira no Kiyomori. It is known as an ancient temple with ties to the Taira clan, and is also the temple where the high priest Jion Sonja was ordained. The Kosaka Kiseki Memorial Museum is also located within the temple grounds.

sights.name: Tsunami and Storm Surge Station
sights.description: This disaster prevention education facility allows visitors to learn about the horrors of tsunamis and high tides through simulated experiences using video and audio, and to acquire knowledge such as proper evacuation methods.

sights.name: Kaiyodo Figure Museum (Miraiza Osaka Castle)
sights.description: This museum displays over 3,000 figures created by Kaiyodo over the course of more than 40 years. You can enjoy the world of sculptures from a variety of genres, including special effects, anime, biology, and art.

sights.name: Yodoyabashi
sights.description: This famous bridge spans the Tosabori River and has been chosen as the most attractive bridge by Osaka residents. The original bridge was built by Yodoya, a wealthy merchant from the Edo period, and is now designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan.

sights.name: Yodogawa River Park
sights.description: This vast park stretches along the Yodo River, from Fukushima Ward to Oyamazaki Town in Kyoto Prefecture. Boasting an area approximately 1.9 times larger than Osaka Castle Park, it's a popular spot for locals, offering abundant nature and well-equipped sports facilities.

sights.name: Yodogawa Shrine
sights.description: Located in Miyakojima Ward, Osaka City, this shrine enshrines fifteen deities, including Amaterasu Omikami. It is a place associated with the haiku poet Yosa Buson, and its summer festival in July is a well-known summer tradition in Miyakojima Ward.

sights.name: Minatomachi River Place
sights.description: A complex where you can enjoy the dynamic cityscape and waterfront atmosphere. It also houses the live music venue "Namba Hatch," restaurants, and an event plaza.

sights.name: Yuki Art Museum
sights.description: This museum houses and exhibits tea ceremony utensils, tea ceremony wares, art pieces, and more collected over a period of 50 years by Yuki Teiichi, the founder of the Japanese restaurant Kitcho.

sights.name: Takimi Koji
sights.description: Located on the first basement floor of Umeda Sky Building, this dining district allows you to enjoy meals in a retro townscape that recreates the early Showa period.

sights.name: Tamatsukuri Inari Shrine
sights.description: In ancient times, the surrounding area was called "Tamatsukurioka" and was inhabited by the Tamakuribe, who made magatama (comma-shaped beads), which is how the current name Tamatsukuri came about.

sights.name: Ikutama Shrine
sights.description: Engishiki Myojin Taisha Shrine is said to have originated as a shrine dedicated to the gods Ikushima and Tarushima at Ishiyamazaki (near present-day Osaka Castle). It is characterized by its main hall, the only one of its kind in Japan, built in the "Ikutama-zukuri" style.

sights.name: Ikune Shrine (Nishinari Ward)
sights.description: This shrine is located in Nishinari Ward, Osaka City. It is known for its blessings in preventing strokes and warding off dementia, and every July it hosts the "Daigaku Festival," a tangible cultural property of Osaka Prefecture, and the "Kotsuma Pumpkin Festival" on the winter solstice.

sights.name: Ikoma Building
sights.description: The headquarters building of Ikoma Watch Shop overlooks Kitahama, the town of stock exchanges. It is a treasure trove of history, full of charm, with a clock tower, sculptures, stained glass, and more.

sights.name: Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma Historical Museum
sights.description: This exhibition introduces the wisdom and future of Japan's pharmaceutical industry, which was nurtured in Doshomachi, along with the history of Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma, which spans more than 345 years.

sights.name: Nanba Betsuin Temple (South Mido Hall) of the Otani branch of Shinshu Buddhism
sights.description: Affectionately known as Minami no Mido-san, this historic temple is the origin of the name Midosuji. There are historical sites such as a stone monument bearing a haiku poem by Matsuo Basho, and Buddhist lectures and events are also held here.

sights.name: Statue of Sanada Yukimura
sights.description: A bronze statue of Sanada Yukimura stands bravely in the grounds of Sanko Shrine. It was erected in 1987 and its base is made of Sanada stone taken from the Sanada family temple. The adjacent "Sanada's Secret Hole" is also a historical attraction.

sights.name: Karabori area
sights.description: This area retains the remnants of the castle town from the time when Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle. It's a popular strolling spot where historical streetscapes and new culture coexist, including "Ren," a complex facility that renovates old townhouses.

sights.name: Tachibana Street (Orange Street)
sights.description: This street, which represents Minami-Horie in Osaka, is lined with stylish stores, including cafes, boutiques, general goods stores, and interior design shops, stretching for 800 meters. Formerly known as a furniture town, it is now a hub where new and old cultures blend together.

sights.name: Umeda Sky Building Koji Kinutani Tenku Art Museum
sights.description: This art museum is located on the 27th floor of Umeda Sky Building. It offers the world's first 3D visual experience that lets you jump into a painting, and exhibits works by Koji Kinutani, created using the fresco technique.

sights.name: Midori Bridge
sights.description: This is one of the bridges that spanned the Sengen River, which flowed through Higashi-Osaka City. Until it was filled in in 1967, it spanned the Koyakaido River, an irrigation canal that connected Nakatakano Kaido.

sights.name: Oimatsu Street
sights.description: Stretching about 1km across Nishitenma from east to west, this is Osaka's representative antique art and art district, with around 90 stores, including antique art dealers and galleries.

sights.name: Higobashi Bridge
sights.description: This ancient bridge spans the Tosabori River, and at its northern end was once the storehouse of the Higo and Kumamoto domains.

sights.name: Maishima Seaside Promenade
sights.description: This stylish promenade offers beautiful views of Minami-ko and Tempozan. The sunset seen from the stepped grass stands is very romantic, and at night, the night view is breathtaking.

sights.name: Maishima Shin-Yuhigaoka
sights.description: A 25m-high artificial hill in Maishima, Osaka. It is a famous spot selected as one of Japan's top 100 sunset spots, and is equipped with an observation plaza and walking paths offering panoramic views of Awaji Island and Kobe Port.

sights.name: Semba Building
sights.description: This building, completed in 1925, conveys the history of modern architecture in Senba, Osaka. It features a distinctive design with a long, patio-like courtyard in the center, an open atrium, and a corridor surrounding it.

sights.name: Shibakawa Building
sights.description: Completed on July 1, 1927, this historic reinforced concrete building is a representative example of Yodoyabashi, Osaka. It features a unique exterior with South American Mayan and Incan decorations and was once used as a bridal school.

sights.name: Basho's haiku monument (Sumiyoshi Park)
sights.description: This monument is engraved with a poem that the haiku poet Matsuo Basho composed when he visited the Takara no Ichi Shinto ritual at Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine in September 1694 (Genroku 7).

sights.name: Hananoi Bridge
sights.description: This bridge was built in 1920 (Taisho 9) across the Edobori River. The bridge's name originates from "Konohana-no-i," a famous spring that Emperor Meiji used as a water source during his visit to Osaka. Currently, a monument stands on the grounds of Osaka Municipal Hananoi Junior High School.

sights.name: Flower Expo Memorial Park Tsurumi Ryokuchi
sights.description: This vast urban park, covering approximately 123 hectares, was redeveloped on the site of the 1990 International Garden and Greenery Exposition.

sights.name: Chayamachi area
sights.description: Osaka's Kita district is the number one youth district, and is a trendsetting area with fashion, miscellaneous goods, cafes, theaters and more.

sights.name: Chausuyama (Tennoji Park)
sights.description: This historical spot was the site of the battles between the Toyotomi and Tokugawa clans during the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka. At 26m above sea level, it is one of the five lowest mountains in Osaka and is also known as the headquarters of Sanada Yukimura.

sights.name: Manpukuji Temple
sights.description: This temple in Tennoji Ward, Osaka City, was founded by Maeda Jirobei Toshinobu, the younger brother of the Sengoku period warlord Maeda Toshiie.

sights.name: Fujita Museum of Art
sights.description: This is a top-class private art museum that houses the collection of Meiji era businessman Fujita Denzaburo, with a collection of approximately 2,000 pieces of ancient Oriental art, including 9 national treasures and 53 important cultural properties.

sights.name: Japan Mint Museum
sights.description: The Mint Museum is housed in a Western-style brick building from the Meiji period, originally constructed as a thermal power plant in 1911. It displays precious coins, orders, medals, and other items from Japan and abroad, and provides a detailed introduction to the minting business.

sights.name: Dotonbori Konamon Museum
sights.description: At the Konamon Food Museum, you can eat, learn, and experience Osaka's soul food, takoyaki. The food sample making experience is particularly popular.

sights.name: Tekijuku
sights.description: This school for Dutch studies was run by Ogata Koan from 1838 to 1862. It produced many great figures of the late Edo period, including Fukuzawa Yukichi, and the building is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan.

sights.name: Nozato Sumiyoshi Shrine
sights.description: The shrine is said to have been founded by Ashikaga Yoshimitsu in 1382. It is known for the "One Night Court Lady" ritual, an intangible cultural property of Osaka Prefecture, and the legend of Iwami Jutaro's slaying of a baboon.

sights.name: Hokonagashi Bridge
sights.description: This bridge spans the Dojima River, connecting the north bank of Nakanoshima with Nishitenma. It is known for the Hokonagara Shinto ritual held every year on the morning of July 24th as part of the Tenjin Festival.

sights.name: Ginzanji Temple
sights.description: Founded in 1591, this Jodo sect temple is located in Tennoji Ward, Osaka City.

sights.name: Nishiki Bridge
sights.description: This pedestrian-only bridge is located on the south side of the Asahi Festival Hall. On top of the bridge, you can see tiled prints of Nishikie art, which remind you of the history of Nakanoshima.

sights.name: Nagahoribashi
sights.description: This was the first bridge built over the Nagahori River, which was excavated in 1625 to connect the Higashiyokobori River and the Kizu River. It once played an important role as a government bridge, and a monument has now been erected there.

sights.name: Nagai Park
sights.description: Osaka's representative comprehensive park, covering an area of 66.3 hectares, is home to a variety of facilities, including Yanmar Stadium Nagai and Nagai Botanical Gardens, and is popular with people of all ages.

sights.name: Abeno Oji Shrine
sights.description: Located south of Tennoji, this shrine was known as the fourth of the 99 Kumano Oji shrines during the Heian period when pilgrimages to Kumano were popular. It is known for its blessings of warding off evil, good health, and recovery from illness.

sights.name: Abeno Shrine
sights.description: Located in Abeno-ku, Osaka City, this shrine enshrines Kitabatake Akiie, a famous general during the Nanboku-cho period, and his father, Kitabatake Chikafusa. Founded in 1885, the shrine hosts a procession ceremony to Kitabatake Park during the summer festival.

sights.name: Namba Yasaka Shrine
sights.description: This shrine, representing Namba, Osaka, is famous for its 12m-tall emaden (votive plaque hall) in the shape of a giant lion's head. It is known as the god of protection from evil and victory, and its tug-of-war ritual has been designated an intangible folk cultural asset by Osaka City.

sights.name: Naniwa Palace Ruins Park
sights.description: The remains of the palaces from the early and late periods of Osaka, which was the capital of Japan from the Asuka to Nara periods, are evidence that Osaka was the capital of Japan.

sights.name: Naniwa Bridge (Lion Bridge)
sights.description: This bridge, which dates back to the Edo period and is affectionately known as "Lion Bridge," is one of Osaka's most iconic bridges.

sights.name: Namba Shrine
sights.description: This ancient shrine in Osaka is said to have been founded by Emperor Hanzei to enshrine his father, Emperor Nintoku. It is known for the distribution of kachiwari ice at the Himuro Festival in July.

sights.name: Tsuyuten Shrine (Ohatsutenjin Shrine)
sights.description: Founded over 1,300 years ago, this shrine is known as the setting for Chikamatsu Monzaemon's "Sonezaki Shinju." It is a power spot in Umeda, Osaka, visited by people praying for fulfillment in love.

sights.name: Utsubo Park
sights.description: This park stretches across approximately 9.7 hectares in Utsubo Honmachi, Osaka's business Hommachi. You can enjoy the city's oldest rose garden, the Utsubo Tennis Center, which is used for international tournaments, and rows of zelkova trees that change with the seasons.

sights.name: Takatsu Shrine
sights.description: This historic shrine in Osaka is dedicated to Emperor Nintoku and is also known as the setting for classic rakugo.

sights.name: Koma Bridge
sights.description: Koraibashi Bridge, which spans the Higashi-Yokobori River, is known as Osaka's first iron bridge, and is a historic bridge where a milepost was placed during the Meiji period, marking the starting point for calculating road distances in western Japan.

sights.name: Fishing Park Embankment (Osaka South Port Fishing Park)
sights.description: The only sea fishing park in Osaka Prefecture. A fishing spot using the breakwater of Nanko Port, you can target a variety of fish species such as horse mackerel, mackerel, and black porgy. Free fishing lessons are also held on weekends.

sights.name: Reienji Temple
sights.description: This temple, located in Tennoji Ward, Osaka City, was founded in 1623.

sights.name: Kitashinchi
sights.description: This high-end entertainment district, representing Osaka's Kita area, has flourished as a place for business people to exchange information. It is an area where you can find a variety of restaurants, including bars, clubs, snack bars, small restaurants, and Japanese and Western cuisine.

sights.name: The Museum of Oriental Ceramics, Osaka
sights.description: The museum houses approximately 5,700 pieces of Oriental ceramics, including the Ataka Collection. This world-class collection, including two national treasures and 13 important cultural properties, can be viewed in beautiful exhibition rooms with natural lighting.

sights.name: Himeshima Shrine
sights.description: This shrine enshrines Akarubihime-no-Mikoto, who is loved as the "goddess of decision-making and action." It also attracts believers as a "start-over shrine" that supports new beginnings and women's independence.

sights.name: Toyokuni Shrine
sights.description: Located on the south side of the main citadel in Osaka Castle Park, this shrine enshrines Hideyoshi, Hideyori, and Hidenaga, and is known as a god for praying for success and good fortune.

sights.name: Mito Shrine
sights.description: It is also called Kumano Shrine because people who traveled along the Amano Kaido road to Kumano in Kishu used to make pilgrimages there.

sights.name: Osaka Prefectural Sayamaike Museum
sights.description: The museum displays 1,400 years of civil engineering and flood control history, with a focus on cultural assets excavated from Sayama Pond, Japan's oldest dam-type reservoir. The building, designed by Tadao Ando, is also a highlight.

sights.name: Osaka Sayama City Local History Museum
sights.description: This museum introduces the historic town of Sayama, showing its transition from ancient times to the present through stone tools, weapons, ancient documents, and more.

sights.name: Sayama Pond
sights.description: Built around 616 AD, it is Japan's oldest dam-type reservoir. Boasting an area of approximately 400,000 square meters, historical figures such as Gyoki and Chogen have been involved in its renovation.

day_to_day.name: Sakai Higashi Tourist Information Center
day_to_day.description: The Sakai-Higashi Tourist Information Center, located at Sakai-Higashi Station on the Nankai Koya Line, meets the diverse needs of customers by providing information on Sakai's tourist facilities and events, and displaying and selling traditional Sakai products.

day_to_day.name: Sakai Station Tourist Information Center
day_to_day.description: We provide tourist information such as the Sakai Tourist Guidebook, bicycle rentals, and luggage storage services. We are a JNTO-certified foreigner information center.

day_to_day.name: Daisen Park Tourist Information Center
day_to_day.description: This tourist information center is located inside the Mozu Kofun Group Visitor Center, adjacent to the Emperor Nintoku Tomb. As a JNTO-certified tourist information center for foreign visitors, it has English-speaking staff on hand.

activities.name: Kanbukuro (walnut rice cakes)
activities.description: This long-established store was founded in the late Kamakura period (1st year of Gentoku). Its specialty "Kurumi Mochi" is a traditional Sakai confection made by wrapping mochi in a secret bean paste.

activities.name: Fenice Sakai (Sakai City Arts and Culture Hall)
activities.description: This arts and culture hub boasts one of the largest halls in southern Osaka, with a capacity of 2,000 seats. It is renowned for its excellent acoustics and accommodates a wide range of performing arts, including music, opera, ballet, and theater.

activities.name: Sakai City Hall 21st floor observation lobby
activities.description: The observation floor is located about 80 meters above ground. There are large observation windows in all directions, and you can enjoy a 360-degree panoramic view, including the Emperor Nintoku Tomb, the largest in the world, for free.

activities.name: Sakai City Fisheries Association Toretoreichi
activities.description: This market is held every Saturday and Sunday at Sakai Dejima Fishing Port. You can buy fresh seafood and enjoy a seafood barbecue on a charcoal grill.

activities.name: Sakai Incense (Baieido Showroom)
activities.description: This showroom allows you to learn about the manufacturing process of incense sticks and their effects, and experience incense, a familiar part of Japanese life, through the spirit of the art of incense.

activities.name: Shrine maiden experience
activities.description: Learn about Japanese Shinto and spiritual culture through the "Miko Experience" at Aikachi Shrine, which has protected this land for over 1,700 years.

sights.name: Strawberry Sakai
sights.description: This urban farm is easily accessible from the nearest station, just a 10-minute walk away. You can enjoy plenty of ripe, fragrant, delicious strawberries.

sights.name: Osaka Sakai Balloon
sights.description: This is a hot air balloon experience attraction that allows you to enjoy a panoramic view of the Mozu Tombs, Osaka Prefecture's only World Heritage Site, including the Emperor Nintoku Tomb, as well as the Sakai cityscape from about 100 meters above the ground.

sights.name: “Sakai Risho no Mori”
sights.description: This museum allows you to experience History / culture of Sakai through the lives and achievements of Sen no Rikyu, the master of tea ceremony born in Sakai, and the poet Yosano Akiko. You can also experience authentic tea ceremony and tour the Sakai Tai-an.

sights.name: Compeito Museum Sakai
sights.description: This facility allows visitors to learn about the history and culture of konpeito (sugar candy), which was introduced from Portugal, and to experience making their own original konpeito in a miniature 30cm diameter pot.

sights.name: Xavier Park
sights.description: This park was built on the site of the residence of Hibiya Ryokei, a wealthy merchant who lavished hospitality on Francis Xavier when he visited Sakai in 1550. It was named to commemorate the 400th anniversary of Xavier's arrival in Japan.

sights.name: Shimano Bicycle Museum
sights.description: This museum uses actual exhibits and videos to introduce the history of bicycles around the world, the dreams of inventors, science, and the future. It also offers test rides and bicycle riding classes for children.

sights.name: Sofia Sakai (Sakai City Education and Culture Center) Planetarium Sakai Starry Sky Museum, where a thousand dreams sparkle
sights.description: Sakai City's only planetarium. Popular attractions include family programs that even families with babies can enjoy, and astronomical observation sessions using one of Osaka Prefecture's largest 60cm reflecting telescopes.

sights.name: Tomb of Emperor Nintoku
sights.description: It is the largest keyhole-shaped tumulus in Japan, measuring approximately 486 meters in length. It is one of the components of the UNESCO World Heritage Site, the Mozu-Furuichi Kofun Group, and is managed by the Imperial Household Agency as the mausoleum of the 16th Emperor, Emperor Nintoku.

sights.name: Nanshuji Temple
sights.description: Buddhist temple in Sakai.

sights.name: clay pagoda
sights.description: This pagoda was built southeast of the Oono-ji temple complex, which was built by the renowned monk Gyoki. It is the only pyramid-shaped, tiled earthen pagoda in Japan. It was designated a national historic site in 1953.

sights.name: Sakai Alphonse Mucha Museum
sights.description: The museum houses works by Alphonse Mucha, a leading Art Nouveau artist, painted throughout his life. It also features works by Akiko Yosano, such as "Myojo" and "Madaregami," and is a museum where you can experience the history of East-West cultural exchange.

sights.name: Sakai Green Museum Harvest Hill
sights.description: Located in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture, this nature-rich agricultural park offers a year-round opportunity for adults and children to interact with plants and animals. Enjoy seasonal flower fields, animal feeding experiences, a Sylvanian park, athletics, and more.

sights.name: Sakai Densho Museum
sights.description: This facility brings together Sakai's traditional industries under one roof, offering exhibitions, sales, and hands-on experiences.

sights.name: Sakai City Museum
sights.description: This museum collects, preserves, and exhibits materials related to the history, art, archaeology, and folklore of Sakai City.

sights.name: Sakai City Big Bang
sights.description: This completely indoor facility is full of fun activities, where you can create, learn, move your body, and more. The main building, which is modeled after a landed spaceship, and the "Tower of Playground Equipment," a giant jungle gym 53 meters above ground, are popular.

sights.name: Sakai City Tea Houses Shinan and Obaian
sights.description: Located in Sakai, the hometown of the tea master Sen no Rikyu, this tea house was designed by the Meiji era master Ogi Rodo in the sukiya style. It is designated as a national registered tangible cultural property, and you can enjoy matcha tea in a ryureiseki style setting.

sights.name: Tajihayahime Shrine
sights.description: Founded around 580, Tajihayahime Shrine enshrines Tajihayahime, Susanoo, and Sugawara no Michizane, and is said to grant blessings for safe childbirth, matchmaking, and protection from evil. The main hall is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan.

sights.name: Daisen Park
sights.description: Located between the tombs of Emperor Nintoku and Emperor Richu, this vast park of approximately 35 hectares includes a lawn plaza, a Japanese garden, and the Sakai City Museum.

sights.name: Daisen Park and Japanese Garden
sights.description: The garden, which makes full use of traditional Japanese garden design techniques and is designed as a strolling garden with a hill, forest and spring, conveys the cultural atmosphere of Sakai.

sights.name: Daianji Temple
sights.description: This Rinzai Zen temple of the Tofuku-ji school was founded in the early Muromachi period by Tokuhide Shigeaki.

sights.name: Mt. Daiho Hounzenji Temple (Hounji Temple)
sights.description: This ancient Obaku sect temple was founded by Zen Master Egoku Domyo in 1672. It is famous for its Daibutsuden Hall, which houses 3,333 Buddha statues, as well as events such as the azaleas in April and the Manto-e festival in August.

sights.name: Kobayashi Museum of Art
sights.description: Oizumi Ryokuchi, which straddles Sakai City and Matsubara City, is one of Osaka's four major green spaces and is decorated with approximately 320,000 flowers and trees of 200 different species.

sights.name: Ohama Park
sights.description: This historic park opened in 1879 (Meiji 12). It features a baseball field, sumo wrestling ring, gymnasium, swimming pool, and monkey island, making it a popular spot for sports and recreation for local residents.

sights.name: Otori Taisha Shrine
sights.description: Known as the Ichinomiya of Izumi Province, this historic shrine enshrines Emperor Yamato Takeru as its main deity.

sights.name: Yamaguchi Family Residence
sights.description: The Yamaguchi Residence is a valuable building, designated as a National Important Cultural Property, as it is one of the few remaining townhouses built in the early Edo period, shortly after the town of Sakai was completely destroyed by fire during the Siege of Osaka.

sights.name: Hochigai Shrine
sights.description: Located on the border of the three countries of Settsu, Kawachi, and Izumi, this shrine has long been worshipped as a god who wards off disasters, and is known for praying for protection from misfortune when building a new house, moving, or traveling.

sights.name: Old Sakai Lighthouse
sights.description: Built in 1877, this lighthouse is one of the oldest Western-style wooden lighthouses still standing in Japan. It has been designated a national historic site and is a beloved symbol of Sakai.

sights.name: Honganji Sakai Betsuin
sights.description: Honganji Sakai Betsuin Temple is the largest wooden building in Sakai City. It was once used as the Sakai Prefectural Office and is now known as the "Sakai Prefectural Office Ruins," a designated historic site of Osaka Prefecture.

sights.name: Sakurai Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is listed in the Engishiki-naisha (Engishiki-listed shrine) in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture.

sights.name: Hodoji Temple
sights.description: This temple was founded in 670 AD (the 9th year of Emperor Tenji's reign) at the behest of Emperor Tenji.

sights.name: Hamadera Park
sights.description: Designated as a public park in 1873, this is one of Osaka's oldest parks. It is a comprehensive park featuring a beautiful pine forest that has been selected as one of Japan's 100 most famous pines, a pool with a giant slide, a rose garden, and more.

sights.name: Hamadera Park Rose Garden
sights.description: Hamadera Park is one of Osaka's oldest prefectural parks, and is home to a vast rose garden covering approximately 2.7 hectares. Approximately 6,000 roses of 500 varieties bloom in a variety of Japanese and Western-style landscapes.

sights.name: Hamadera Park Old Station Building
sights.description: The half-timbered wooden station building was designed by Tatsuno Kingo and Kataoka Yasushi in 1907. It is designated as a national tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Seigakuin
sights.description: It has a history as a training center for Shugendo sects, and is a registered tangible cultural property of Japan.

sights.name: Shirasagi Park Iris Garden
sights.description: This is a famous spot where the iris, the official flower of Sakai City, beautifully colors the cloudy skies of the rainy season. Approximately 150 varieties and 10,000 irises bloom in the 90,000 square meter grounds from late May to early June.

sights.name: Mozu Hachiman Shrine
sights.description: Mozu Hachimangu Shrine is located in the heart of the Mozu Kofun Group and was founded approximately 1,400 years ago during the reign of Emperor Kinmei.

sights.name: Mozu Kofun Group
sights.description: This World Heritage Site is located in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture. It is a group of 44 ancient tombs, including the Emperor Nintoku Tomb, and huge keyhole-shaped tombs built between the end of the 4th century and the second half of the 6th century.

sights.name: Shounji Temple
sights.description: This temple boasts a beautiful dry landscape garden with white sand arranged to resemble flowing water. Founded by Takuan Soho, it features a nationally designated Important Cultural Property and a scenic garden designated by Osaka Prefecture.

sights.name: Sugawara Shrine
sights.description: Sugawara Shrine is affectionately known as "Sakai's Tenjin-san." It enshrines Sugawara no Michizane as its deity, and within its grounds are Sakai Ebisu Shrine and Japan's oldest Yakuso Shrine. The Niomon Gate is a tangible cultural property designated by Osaka Prefecture.

sights.name: Sugao Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is one of the shrines listed in the Engishiki (an ancient Japanese legal code). It enshrines Tenjin (Sugawara no Michizane), and its grounds contain "Sugazawa," which is said to be the birthplace of Michizane.

sights.name: Hagiwara Tenjin (Hagiwara Shrine)
sights.description: This historic shrine in Sakai City is said to have originated over 1,000 years ago as a shrine dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane. Within the shrine grounds, the former main hall, which dates back approximately 350 years and faithfully retains the Momoyama style, is preserved and open to the public.

sights.name: Tourist Farm Minami Rakuen
sights.description: Located in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture, this vast tourist farm was reclaimed in 1931. In addition to experiencing seasonal fruit and vegetable harvesting, you can also enjoy barbecues, a fishing pond, and athletics.

sights.name: Gunsmith House
sights.description: The only remaining workshop and residence of a gunsmith from the Edo period in Japan. Designated a tangible cultural property by Sakai City.

sights.name: Akaguchi Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is said to have been built by order of Empress Jingu to protect the entrance to Osaka Bay and is the guardian deity of Izumi Sakai Minami-sho (Sakai's main guardian deity). It is also known as the inner sanctuary of Sumiyoshi.

sights.name: Takabayashi Family Residence
sights.description: It is one of the oldest private houses in Osaka Prefecture. Its current form was completed over 200 years ago during the Kansei era. It is a valuable historical building that retains the layout of a village headman's residence from the Edo period in the Kinki region.

sights.name: Kurohimeyama Tomb
sights.description: The Kurohimeyama Kofun is a keyhole-shaped burial mound measuring 114 meters in length, 64 meters in width at the front, and 11 meters in height.

sights.name: Ichioka Shrine
sights.description: Ichioka Shrine, affectionately known as "Kaiei-gu" or "Gion-san," is a spot dedicated to academic success, worshiping the god of wisdom, Takehaya Susanoo-no-Mikoto, as its main deity. Within the shrine grounds are the ruins of Kaikai-ji Temple, a nationally designated historic site.

sights.name: Sennan Marble Beach

sights.name: Otoko Shrine (Ono Shrine)
sights.description: Otoko Shrine, located in Sennan City, Osaka Prefecture, is a former Engishiki shrine with a history dating back to before Christ. It enshrines Itsutsu no Mikoto and is also known as Otakebi no Miya.

sights.name: Tanekawa Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is located in Sennan City, Osaka Prefecture. It has a history of calming a smallpox epidemic that swept through prayers in 1545, and is now cherished as the main shrine of the region. It is also famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot in spring, when approximately 100 cherry trees bloom.

sights.name: EXPOCITY
sights.description: The fun of "playing, learning, and discovering" all in one place! This large-scale complex includes the NIFREL Museum of Living Creatures, Japan's tallest Ferris wheel, and Mitsui Shopping Park LaLaport EXPOCITY, which has around 300 stores.

sights.name: OSAKA WHEEL
sights.description: At 123 meters tall, it's the largest Ferris wheel in Japan. All gondolas have see-through floors, and you can enjoy the view of Osaka from a comfortable, air-conditioned space.

sights.name: Asahi Beer Museum
sights.description: This experiential museum, based on the concept of "a place where you can encounter the best, most memorable beer," allows you to experience the world of Asahi Beer with all five senses. You can enjoy VR experiences, videos of the manufacturing process, tastings, and more.

sights.name: Duskin Museum
sights.description: The facility consists of two spaces: the Cleaning Hall, where you can learn about the history of cleaning, and the Mister Donut Museum, where you can learn about the history of Mister Donut and even try making donuts.

sights.name: The Living Museum: NIFREL
sights.description: This "living museum" is a unique genre that combines an aquarium, zoo, and art museum, with the concept of "touching the senses."

sights.name: Expo ’70 Commemorative Park
sights.description: This cultural park was built on the site of the 1970 World Exposition (Osaka Expo). You can enjoy the Tower of the Sun, seasonal flowers, athletic facilities, the EXPO '70 Pavilion, and more.

sights.name: Saidera Temple
sights.description: This historic temple was founded by Gyoki. It is known for its bell tower, which retains the style of the early Edo period, the holy water "Sai no Shimizu" that is said to be effective for eye ailments, and the "Cucumber Kaji" ceremony held on the day of the Ox during the Dog Days.

sights.name: Kishibe Shrine
sights.description: Located on Mt. Shikinzan in Suita City, Osaka Prefecture, this shrine is known for its magnificent Momoyama-style shrine building, a restoration of an important cultural property, and for the "Donji" ritual, a city-designated intangible folk cultural property.

sights.name: National Museum of Ethnology
sights.description: Located in Osaka's Expo'70 Commemorative Park, this is one of the world's largest ethnological museums, with a focus on cultural anthropology and ethnology. It houses approximately 345,000 items, including everyday items and ethnic costumes collected by researchers from around the world.

sights.name: Tarumi Shrine
sights.description: Tarumi Shrine is located in Suita City, Osaka Prefecture. The shrine's name, "Tarumi," means "water flowing down a cliff," and it has been worshipped as the god of water since ancient times.

sights.name: Japan Folk Crafts Museum, Osaka
sights.description: Located within Expo'70 Commemorative Park, this museum displays exquisite crafts from Japan and around the world, including ceramics, dyed textiles, and paintings. It occupies the space of a pavilion from the 1970 World Exposition in Japan.

sights.name: Former Nishio Residence (Suita Cultural Creation Exchange Center)
sights.description: This modern Japanese-style building was once used by village headmen during the Edo period.

sights.name: Izumidono Shrine
sights.description: This shrine in Suita City, Osaka Prefecture, was founded in 869.

sights.name: Mount Pompon
sights.description: This 678.8m-high mountain was named after the "ponpon" sound that can be heard when you stomp on its summit. Located on the border between Takatsuki City, Osaka Prefecture and Kyoto Prefecture, the hiking trail along the Tokai Nature Trail is popular.

sights.name: Shinike Haniwa Factory Park Historic Site
sights.description: This park preserves and maintains the Shinike ruins, the site of Japan's oldest and largest haniwa factory. This is where the haniwa for the Imashirozuka Tomb were manufactured, and visitors can tour the restored kilns and workshops for free.

sights.name: Settsukyo Park
sights.description: This 42.65 hectare scenic park stretches across the upper reaches of the Akutagawa River in the northern part of Takatsuki City. The valley, lined with oddly shaped rocks and cliffs, is known as "Settsu Yabakei" and has been selected as one of Osaka's 100 best green spaces.

sights.name: Honzanji Temple
sights.description: This ancient Tendai sect temple boasts numerous treasures, and the clear mountain air and tranquility cleanse the souls of visitors. It is said to have been founded by En no Gyoja and later established by Prince Kaisei in the 8th century.

sights.name: Kabusanji Temple
sights.description: This ancient temple has a history of 1,300 years and is the first in Japan to house Bishamonten. Homa prayers are held every day without fail, and it is a famous spot where you can see fresh greenery in the spring and vibrant colors of the leaves in the fall.

sights.name: Basho's haiku monument (Tamagawa Village)
sights.description: This monument, inscribed with the haiku of the haiku poet Matsuo Basho, reads, "Unohana ya akuraki willow no morigoshi." Located in a scenic spot known as Tamagawa in Mishima, Settsu Province, the unohana flowers bloom in full glory in early summer.

sights.name: Nomi Shrine
sights.description: This historic shrine in Takatsuki City, Osaka Prefecture, was founded during the Heian period to quell epidemics. It was revered by successive lords of Takatsuki Castle as its guardian deity.

sights.name: Takatsuki City Natural History Museum Aquapia Akutagawa
sights.description: This museum introduces the waterfront of the Akutagawa River, which flows through the center of Takatsuki City, as well as the local nature and history. It features a large aquarium displaying freshwater fish, and a wide selection of stuffed and specimen birds, plants, and insects.

sights.name: Yamabikoen
sights.description: This tourist farm is nestled in the quiet mountains of Tondabayashi City, Osaka Prefecture. In addition to mandarin orange picking, sweet potato digging, and chestnut gathering in the fall, you can enjoy barbecues year-round.

sights.name: Nakamura Family Residence
sights.description: This townhouse was built around 1782 in Jinanimachi. It once operated as a sake brewery called "Sadoya," and Yoshida Shoin also stayed there. It is now a designated cultural property of Osaka Prefecture, and still retains the merchant style of the time. *The interior is not open to the public.

sights.name: Shiroyama Orange Garden
sights.description: This is an experiential farm where people of all ages can enjoy the whole day, with activities such as fruit picking (mandarin oranges, sweet potato digging, and chestnut gathering), handmade play equipment, barbecues, crayfish fishing, and mini golf.

sights.name: Tondabayashi Jinanimachi
sights.description: This area is designated as an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings by the national government, and retains the town layout of the late Middle Ages. It is lined with historic houses, retaining the appearance of a religious autonomous city from the Sengoku period.

sights.name: Tondabayashi City Agricultural Park (Savor Farm)
sights.description: This vast agricultural park in Tondabayashi City, Osaka Prefecture, is scheduled to reopen on August 2, 2025, where you can enjoy seasonal fruit and vegetable harvesting and BBQs.

sights.name: Important Cultural Property Former Sugiyama Residence
sights.description: This merchant's residence is the oldest townhouse in Tondabayashi Jinanimachi and is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. During the Edo period, it developed as a sake brewery and is also known as the birthplace of the poet Ishigami Tsuyuko.

sights.name: Nansoan Kannonji Temple
sights.description: This temple is said to have been built by Kusunoki Masashige's wife, Hisako (Haikyouni), to commemorate the souls of her family. It is a historic spot where you can enjoy the magnificent autumn foliage.

sights.name: Takitani Fudo Myo-o Temple
sights.description: This historic prayer hall was founded by Kobo Daishi during the Heian period. It is counted as one of Japan's three most important Fudo temples and is known for its blessings of business prosperity and protection from evil.

sights.name: Migukurumitama Shrine
sights.description: The name "Migukurumitama" comes from the fact that the shrine enshrines "Mikukurumitama," the god who controls water and distributes water from the mountains to the land. It was founded by Emperor Sujin and the enshrined deity is Okuninushi no Mikoto.

sights.name: Nishikiori Shrine
sights.description: The main hall, believed to have been founded in 1363, is a nationally designated Important Cultural Property. Situated in a historic area once known as Baekje Village, it preserves the culture and weaving techniques of immigrants to the present day.

sights.name: Ryusenji Temple
sights.description: This ancient Shingon Buddhist temple is associated with the story of Soga no Umako's slaying of an evil dragon, and it also has a beautiful strolling garden with a pond decorated with seasonal flowers.

sights.name: Sumiyoshi Shrine (also known as Wakamiya Sumiyoshi Shrine)
sights.description: This shrine originated from Itsukushima Shrine, founded by Taira no Kiyomori, on the site of Ishirenji Temple, which was established by Gyoki during the Tenpyo era. It is revered as the guardian shrine of Kosone-go in Toyonaka City.

sights.name: Senri Tenjin (Kamishinden Tenjin Shrine)
sights.description: The local deity of Senri. The main deity is Tenjin-sama (Michizane Sugawara), the god of academics, and the co-enshrined deity is Inari-o-kami, the god of business prosperity.

sights.name: Museum of Osaka University
sights.description: This museum displays academic specimens from Osaka University, housed in the Machikaneyama Shugakukan building completed in 1931. Its highlights include one of the world's largest crocodile fossils and materials related to Tekijuku and Kaitokudo.

sights.name: Open-Air Museum of Old Japanese Farm Houses
sights.description: Located within Hattori Ryokuchi Park in Toyonaka City, this is Japan's first open-air museum. It displays 12 representative Edo-period houses from all over Japan that have been relocated and restored.

sights.name: Hattori Ryokuchi Park
sights.description: This is a sports and recreation hub in Hokusetsu, with a variety of facilities including an urban greening botanical garden, an outdoor music hall, a Japanese folk house museum, a horse riding center, and a swimming pool.

sights.name: Toko-in Temple of Hagi
sights.description: This temple has a history of 1,300 years, and was founded by Gyoki in 735. It is known as the "Temple of Hagi" because of the approximately 3,000 bush clovers that bloom in the fall.

sights.name: Kyuhoji Jinanimachi
sights.description: This historic townscape still retains the layout from 470 years ago. Jinanimachi was formed around Kenshoji Temple, and the grid-like roads remain as they were back then.

sights.name: Jokoji Temple
sights.description: Jokoji Temple in Yao City, Osaka Prefecture, is known as the birthplace of Kawachi Ondo and has been selected as one of the "Top 100 Soundscapes of Japan." It is famous for its bloody ceiling, which tells the story of the Summer Siege of Osaka, and for its connection to Ashikaga Yoshimitsu.

sights.name: Kusumoto Shrine
sights.description: This shrine is one of the shrines listed in the Engishiki (an ancient Japanese legal code), and it is said that Mononobe no Moriya enshrined it as the guardian deity of Inamura Castle. It has been revered since ancient times as a god of healing from illness, agriculture, and martial arts.

sights.name: Prefectural Forest (Mizunomi Park)
sights.description: This park is rich in nature and offers a panoramic view of the Osaka Plain, as well as one of the prefecture's largest hydrangea and azalea gardens.
